info.title: Totalis Hyperliquid API
info.description:
REST API for Totalis singles and parlays on Hyperliquid HIP-4 outcome markets, for client integrations and external market makers.

There are three ways in, each sent as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`:

- **Scoped API key** (`ttk_`), for servers, bots and market makers. The account owner creates it in the Totalis app, or a wallet-session user creates one with `POST /v1/me/api-keys` and a fresh wallet signature (see API keys). It acts for one account, yours or a maker's, with only the scopes it holds, and needs no `Origin`.
- **Wallet session**, for users who bring their own wallet to a partner's web page. The page signs the wallet in with `POST /v1/auth/wallet-challenges` and `POST /v1/auth/wallet-sessions`; the session is bound to the page's registered `Origin` and must be sent from it. Pages may also label their traffic with their publishable browser key in `X-Totalis-Partner: tpb_...`.
- **Partner server key** (`tpk_`), only for `POST /v1/partner/wallet-admissions`, which lets a new wallet open its account during the invite-only launch, `GET /v1/partner/report`, your fees, terms and payouts, `GET /v1/partner/fills`, each fee event on your users' positions, `GET /v1/partner/webhook-events`, the webhook events Totalis queued for you, and `GET /v1/partner/accounts/{wallet}/account-value`, the value of an account you admitted. Server to server, never in a browser, and never with an `Origin`.

Public market reads need no credential. A credential only authenticates: every bet, cash-out and withdrawal also carries the wallet or maker signature the HyperEVM contract verifies. An external wallet sends `POST /v1/core-exits` to move its vault cash to HyperCore before a HyperCore order.

For access, partner credentials (origins, browser and server keys), builder codes or staging, email [founders@totalis.trade](mailto:founders@totalis.trade).

Amounts are base-10 strings in native USDC atomic units, large identifiers are decimal strings, and every command `POST` requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Every error is `{error: {code, message, retry, request_id, field_violations}}`. `code` is stable; each operation lists the codes it returns per status. `retry` is `NEVER` (stop), `BACKOFF` (resend the same request with the same `Idempotency-Key` after `Retry-After` seconds) or `REFRESH` (re-read state, then send a new request with a new key). `field_violations` names invalid inputs by JSON pointer, such as `/legs/0/side`.

get.description:
List active questions with their titles and markets, and the standalone markets that belong to no question.

No API key required.

200.description: One page of display groups. A `QUESTION` item carries the question's `title` and its outcomes in `markets`; a `STANDALONE` item carries one market that belongs to no question, never a made-up question. Native market state controls visibility: during a reference outage items stay readable with unavailable prices and trading disabled, and informational dates do not close markets. Filtering may return a short or empty page while `has_more` is true; only a null `next_cursor` ends the list. `GET /v1/markets` and `GET /v1/markets/{outcome_id}` keep the complete supported catalog.

get.description:
List active markets as one flat list, one HIP-4 outcome per item; `GET /v1/discovery` groups them under their questions' titles.

No API key required.

parameters.name: eligibility
parameters.description: Keep only markets whose current eligibility.status is this value: ENABLED for markets that accept new positions now, DISABLED for the rest. Eligibility is live, so a market can change status between pages. The filter applies after paging, so a page can be short or empty while has_more is true; next_cursor being null is the only terminal signal. The cursor is bound to this filter.

parameters.name: combo
parameters.description: Keep only markets whose current combo.status is this value: OPEN for markets a Combo may take as a leg now, CLOSED for the rest. Combo status is live: a market opens when it enters its 7-day window and closes when its event starts, so it can change status between pages. The filter applies after paging, so a page can be short or empty while has_more is true; next_cursor being null is the only terminal signal. The cursor is bound to this filter. Combine with eligibility=ENABLED for markets a Combo can include now.

200.description: One page of active markets in one flat list, not grouped by question. Each market is one HIP-4 outcome with its YES and NO sides, its own `title` and its `native_question_id`, but not the question's title; fallback and settled outcomes are left out. Rows leave out metadata_revision and the result's recorded_at_block and evidence_digest; read GET /v1/markets/{outcome_id} for them. A listed market is not a promise that an RFQ on it will be quoted or accepted.

get.description:
Get one market with its YES and NO sides, product details, current round and 24-hour stats.

No API key required.

200.description: The market with its YES and NO sides, product details, current round and 24-hour stats.

content.title: HYPE touches 100 by 20261001-0000
content.rules: The market resolves to Yes if the HYPE price touches 100 at or before 20261001-0000, and otherwise resolves to No. The price counts as touched once the 1-second TWAP of HYPE-USDC perp mark  price equals or crosses 100 at any time after this market is deployed and at or before 20261001-0000; the market can settle as soon as a touch occurs. If HYPE is delisted before this market settles, the HYPE settlement price at delisting counts as the final price for the touch determination, and the market can settle at delisting if the price has not touched 100 by then. metadata=category:price|subCategory:N/A|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to the price of a Hyperliquid perp.

get.description:
Anyone: page a market's taker orders from the account index, newest block first in whole HyperCore blocks, the same events with the same ids as the market stream's trades frames, for history below a tradesSnapshot's complete_from_height; a signed-out answer is the same for everyone and cached for 30 seconds.

No API key required; callers without one receive the public projection. A key, when sent, must be one of:

- a key for your account
- a key for a maker

A wallet session for the account also works, with no scope limit, sent from its `Origin`.

parameters.name: before_height
parameters.description: First page only, instead of cursor: start below this HyperCore height, such as a tradesSnapshot's complete_from_height. Without both, the page starts at the newest order the account index holds, which trails our node by about a second (through_height). A height above the index's through_height + 1 answers 503 DEPENDENCY_STALE, never stored, until the index reaches it: the heights between are in neither the stream nor the index yet, so retry after Retry-After. One at or below the index's floor, below which it holds nothing, answers 400 INVALID_QUERY naming before_height.

200.description: A page of taker orders in whole blocks, at most limit unless its first block alone holds more

Cache-Control.description: public, max-age=30 for a signed-out read; no-store for one with a credential.

items.description: Taker orders of both tokens of the outcome, newest block first and each block's orders in execution order, as trades frames carry them.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when the index holds no older order it can tell.

has_more.description: Whether older indexed fills follow: the next page then holds at least one order, or names unknown_through_height when the next block cannot be told yet.

unknown_through_height.description: Set when the page stopped above fills indexed before the index recorded which side crossed the book: taker orders at and below this height cannot be told until an import fills that in. Null otherwise.

through_height.description: The account index's height: every taker order at or below it, outside gaps, is indexed.

gaps.description: Heights in the span this page answers for (down to its oldest block while has_more, else to unknown_through_height + 1 or the index's floor) that the account index does not hold yet: orders there may be missing until it is repaired.

get.description:
Name and picture up to 100 outcomes from their IDs alone, live or departed, such as the legs of a position or the fills of an account.

No API key required.

200.description: Each asked outcome Totalis recorded with its English title, its native definition exactly as Hyperliquid listed it, and finished pictures for each place it is drawn, resolved from the published imagery manifest. Pictures are decoration: they never carry prices, state or results. IDs Totalis holds no definition of are in `not_recorded`; IDs newer than every outcome it recorded are in `pending`.

Cache-Control.description: Shared caches may reuse an answer with an imagery publication and nothing pending for 60 seconds; any other answer is no-store.

get.description:
Anyone: get one chance or perp mark line on a grid the server picks, reduced for drawing, whose recorded part never changes.

No API key required.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: A window ending now (or at the line's end): Live is the last 60 seconds, 1W 7 days, 1M 30 days, ALL the line's whole record from its first recorded value (with `market`, that market's chance line's), at least 60 seconds.

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Only with a `mark:` line: the outcome id of the market it is drawn for. Its `end` is then that market's expiry or recorded settlement, as for the market's own chance line, and `range=ALL` starts at that market's first record instead of the coin's; other windows are unchanged.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of an explicit window, with to: UTC to the second, as `2026-11-18T19:30:00Z`, on the grid step its span picks (the span at most 366 days), not before 2026-10-18.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of an explicit window, with from, in the same spelling and on the same step, after from and at most a day from now.

200.description: The line on the server's grid. Totalis records every change of a chance or perp mark: second detail for seven days, minute detail from 2026-10-18 18:53 UTC on, forever. The grid's step is the shortest of a fixed ladder (250 ms up to 28 days, aligned to Unix time) that covers the window in at most 240 buckets. A step under a minute draws second detail while the window's first day of it is kept (until eight days after that day's start, and not before Totalis began recording the line's feed); otherwise the window comes on a one-minute grid of minute closes. Each bucket carries the first, lowest, highest and last value it saw at their real times, in time order, and where the line became unknown; a value held into a bucket shows at its start. Everything before `through` is final; continue the bucket that holds it from live points at or after `through`, and the result equals a later read. A line with no record is empty, never a guessed value, and nothing before 2026-10-18 18:53 UTC is drawn.

Cache-Control.description: 60 seconds on minute grids and one bucket (at least a second) on finer ones. A window recorded through its end (a line whose end is final, settled, or a window in the past): an hour while that end is under seven days old, then a day. Until Totalis finished backfilling chance minutes before the first minute it recorded chance live, a chance line's ALL window and any window reaching that minute, also for a mark line read for a market, and a line cut at an end from its expiry alone (final false, a postponement can still move it) keep the minute or bucket age. Never past grid.valid_until or the drop of the second detail it was drawn from, even when that leaves max-age=0. Errors are never stored.

delete.description:
Cancel all of your open quotes when you stop quoting, as Cancel quote would one at a time, leaving up any quote whose acceptance awaits your answer.

Requires a key for a maker with `quote:write`.

200.description: How many quotes this call cancelled, and how many it left under a pending acceptance: confirm or decline those, or let them time out. Takers see each cancelled quote leave as `QUOTE_REMOVED` with status `CANCELLED`; publish again to come back. Send no `Idempotency-Key`: a repeat cancels whatever is open then.

409.description:
A quote can be accepted once: a new `Idempotency-Key` on an RFQ that already has a live acceptance returns `STATE_CONFLICT`, or `ACCEPTANCE_IN_FLIGHT` while an entry acceptance awaits its maker or its trade. An account has one entry acceptance in flight at a time, so accepting any other entry quote meanwhile returns `ACCEPTANCE_IN_FLIGHT` too.

- `QUOTE_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` (retry `REFRESH`): The maker's current capacity does not cover the quote.

- `CORE_MOVE_IN_FLIGHT` (retry `REFRESH`): A HyperCore transfer for this account is still in flight.
- `ACCEPTANCE_IN_FLIGHT` (retry `REFRESH`): Another entry acceptance by this account still awaits its maker or its trade, and an account has one in flight at a time. Nothing was created; once that acceptance's operation ends, accept a fresh quote.

Requires a key for your account with `funding:withdraw`, `sponsorship:use`.

A wallet session for the account also works, with no scope limit, sent from its `Origin`.

202.description: Core exit durably accepted, not yet on chain: follow it with `GET /v1/core-exits/{exit_id}` until `CREDITED`. An exact replay of the same `Idempotency-Key` and body returns the stored exit before any dependency check.

400.description:
The `Idempotency-Key` is a UUIDv7 and becomes the exit ID. Sign the Exit with `account` the credential's account wallet and `to` `deployment.router_address` from `GET /v1/me/core-exits`, and expiry at most `maximum_life_seconds` ahead; a signature over other terms is `INVALID_REQUEST`. A wallet-only account under the minimum, or an activating exit under 2 USDC, names `/amount`.

- `INVALID_REQUEST` (retry `NEVER`): The body, a path parameter or a header is malformed or fails validation. `field_violations` names invalid body fields. `NEVER` means the same request will fail again.
- `INVALID_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` (retry `NEVER`): The command needs exactly one lowercase UUIDv7 `Idempotency-Key` header; confirm and cancel RFQ take none.
- `ORIGIN_REQUIRED` (retry `NEVER`): A browser route needs exactly one `Origin` header.

get.description:
Open the WebSocket that streams your account's or your maker's updates.

Requires one of:

- a key for your account with `account:stream`
- a key for a maker with `rfq:read`
- a key for a maker with `vault:read`
- a key for a maker with `quote:read`
- a key for your account with `rfq:read`

Also requires `replay:read` to resume from a cursor or replay retained events.

A wallet session for the account also works, with no scope limit, sent from its `Origin`.

Each key receives only the frames its scopes allow, and other frame classes are denied:

| Frames | Key | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open RFQ discovery | key for your account | `rfq:read` |
| Account | key for your account | `account:stream` |
| RFQ | key for a maker | `rfq:read` |
| Quote | key for a maker | `quote:read` |
| Account | key for a maker | `vault:read` |

101.description: Switching protocols. Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer`; browsers request the `totalis.realtime.v2` subprotocol plus `auth.<base64url-access-token>` instead. Then send one `subscribe` frame: `account` with a key for your account, or `maker` with a key for a maker and its `maker_id`. The stream answers with a `subscriptionResponse`, then a snapshot or a replay from your cursor, then live events, every frame tagged by `channel`. The server closes the connection when your maker's membership or controller changes; reconnect to continue.

500.description: - `INTERNAL_ERROR` (retry `BACKOFF`): Something failed on Totalis's side that no dependency or input explains, such as a bug or a broken invariant; it is logged with its cause under `request_id`. Retry after Retry-After with the same idempotency key; if it persists, report the `request_id`.

error.description: The error this operation returns with this status.

code.description: One of the registered codes listed in this response's description.

retry.description: The retry rule the registry fixes for the returned code.

503.description:
- `AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE` (retry `BACKOFF`): Identity or credential authority storage is unavailable.
- `DEPENDENCY_STALE` (retry `BACKOFF`): A projection or upstream the request depends on (chain projection, HyperCore state, database) is behind its freshness bound or unavailable.
- `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` (retry `BACKOFF`): The account-read or stream source is unavailable.
- `CONTRACT_UNAVAILABLE` (retry `BACKOFF`): This producer is disabled in this environment.

error.description: The error this operation returns with this status.

code.description: One of the registered codes listed in this response's description.

retry.description: The retry rule the registry fixes for the returned code.

AcceptanceIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
AcceptanceIdempotencyKey.description: Lowercase UUIDv7 that names this acceptance: it becomes the `acceptance_id`. Choose it before the first send and reuse it on every retry. The same key, quote and body returns the stored acceptance without restarting its deadline; the same key with another quote or body returns `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Keys are unique per taker account, across all quotes. A quote can be accepted once: a new key on an RFQ that already has a live acceptance returns `409 STATE_CONFLICT`, or `409 ACCEPTANCE_IN_FLIGHT` while an entry acceptance awaits its maker or its trade; the same answer refuses any other entry quote the account accepts meanwhile. Lost the response? Read `GET /v1/quotes/{quote_id}/acceptance` instead of accepting again.

ActivityKindQueryOptional.name: kind
ActivityKindQueryOptional.description: Return only activities of this kind.

ActivityOrderQueryOptional.name: order
ActivityOrderQueryOptional.description: PUBLISHED (default): newest published first, so a backfilled activity appears on a fresh first page. OCCURRED: newest occurrence first, an activity of unknown occurrence at its recording time, then by activity ID. What reads as one lists together at its latest occurrence (an order's fills, one outcome side's settlement credits, one position's settlement and claims), one group after another within a moment.

ActivityStatusQueryOptional.name: status
ActivityStatusQueryOptional.description: Return only activities with this status. A status-filtered page is a display view, never a balance or P&L basis.

ActivityVenueQueryOptional.name: venue
ActivityVenueQueryOptional.description: Return only activities with evidence from this source: HYPEREVM (EVM logs), HYPERCORE (Hyperliquid ledger) or VENUE (Totalis workflows).

Category.name: category
Category.description: Platform taxonomy category slug. The cursor is bound to this filter.

CollateralReductionJobId.name: job_id
CollateralReductionJobId.description: Collateral-reduction job ID returned when the job was created.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Omit for the first page; then send the previous response's next_cursor unchanged.

DetailContract.name: contract
DetailContract.description: Browse contract of the detail. 4 adds game, the market's game with up to 256 current members, estimated_live_until and scoreboard, the in-play window end and live game reading of the market's matchup, and series_id for IPO ladder members; 2, 3 or omitted return the earlier detail. Only this query parameter selects it, so a browser read needs no CORS preflight; the X-Totalis-Browse-Contract header is ignored on this route. Repeated, malformed or other values return 400 UNSUPPORTED_BROWSE_CONTRACT.

From.name: from
From.description: Inclusive RFC3339 window start. Omit from and to together for the exact rolling 24 hours ending at server time; supplying only one is rejected. The response repeats the resolved bounds, which later pages must reuse.

FromQueryOptional.name: from
FromQueryOptional.description: Inclusive RFC3339 lower bound on occurred_at (recorded_at for workflow entries without one). Chain activity whose occurrence time is unknown is always included.

FromQueryRequired.name: from
FromQueryRequired.description: Inclusive RFC3339 start of the performance period.

HistoryIncludeGaps.name: include_gaps
HistoryIncludeGaps.description: Include at most 1440 retained diagnostic gap records; gaps is empty unless this is true.

HistoryLimit.name: limit
HistoryLimit.description: The shared page limit with one exception: the maximum is 1,440, a full 24-hour window of one-minute bars, so a chart loads in one request.

HistorySeries.name: series
HistorySeries.description: Use `REFERENCE_PRICE_OHLC` for a line chart and `TRADE_OHLCV` for candles; `AUTO` uses trades when there are any. AUTO selects retained closed trade buckets in the window, otherwise reference history. REFERENCE_PRICE_OHLC prefers L2, then BBO, then allMids among sources with a closed bucket in the window; with none it carries the most recent earlier source inside the 90-day online window, breaking ties in that order. With no evidence the empty reference response is labelled L2/BOOK_MID. Explicit series avoids AUTO switching when trades arrive.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Lowercase UUIDv7 naming this command, unique per caller and route. A retry with the same key and body returns the original result; the same key with a different body returns `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.

KeyId.name: key_id
KeyId.description: ID of a key on this account, from the key list or the create response.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum items per page, 1 to 200, default 50. A page may hold fewer, even none, while has_more is true.

MakerId.name: maker_id
MakerId.description: On-chain maker ID, as a decimal string. The credential must be authorized for this maker.

MakerIdPathRequired.name: maker_id
MakerIdPathRequired.description: On-chain maker ID, as a decimal string. An API key may only name the maker it is bound to; other makers return 404.

OperationId.name: operation_id
OperationId.description: Deterministic 32-byte operation ID, as lowercase hex, returned when the command was admitted.

OutcomeId.name: outcome_id
OutcomeId.description: HIP-4 outcome ID of the market, as a decimal string.

OutcomeIds.name: outcome_ids
OutcomeIds.description: 1 to 100 HIP-4 outcome IDs as decimal strings, comma-separated, strictly ascending, so one set of outcomes is always one URL. Any other order, a repeat or an ID above 4294967295 is 400 INVALID_QUERY.

PnlRangeQueryOptional.name: range
PnlRangeQueryOptional.description: Window of the series: 1D, 1W, 1M (default) or ALL since tracking began.

PositionId.name: position_id
PositionId.description: Position ID: the contract's ticketId of the position, as lowercase bytes32 hex.

PositionIdPathRequired.name: position_id
PositionIdPathRequired.description: Position ID: the contract's ticketId (lowercase bytes32 hex).

PositionIdQueryOptional.name: position_id
PositionIdQueryOptional.description: Return only activities that reference this position ID (lowercase bytes32 hex).

PositionMakerResultQueryOptional.name: maker_result
PositionMakerResultQueryOptional.description: Return only positions the maker closed with this result: WON, LOST or EVEN (see maker_result).

PositionOutcomeQueryOptional.name: outcome_id
PositionOutcomeQueryOptional.description: Return only positions with a leg on this HIP-4 outcome, resolved or not.

PositionStatusQueryOptional.name: status
PositionStatusQueryOptional.description: Return only positions with this lifecycle status.

QuoteHistoryFromQueryRequired.name: from
QuoteHistoryFromQueryRequired.description: Inclusive RFC3339 start of the period on submitted_at.

QuoteHistoryStatusQueryOptional.name: status
QuoteHistoryStatusQueryOptional.description: Return only quotes with this status. The fill rate ignores it.

QuoteHistoryThroughQueryRequired.name: through
QuoteHistoryThroughQueryRequired.description: Exclusive RFC3339 end of the period; must be after from.

QuoteId.name: quote_id
QuoteId.description: The quote's `quote_id`, from `QUOTE_CREATED`, `QUOTE_ACCEPTED` or Create quote.

QuoteKindQueryOptional.name: kind
QuoteKindQueryOptional.description: Return, and compute the fill rate over, only quotes of this kind.

RfqId.name: rfq_id
RfqId.description: The RFQ's `rfq_id`, from Create RFQ or `RFQ_CREATED`.

Side.name: side
Side.description: Outcome side whose price history is returned.

Subcategory.name: subcategory
Subcategory.description: Platform taxonomy subcategory slug. The cursor is bound to this filter.

ThroughQueryOptional.name: through
ThroughQueryOptional.description: Exclusive RFC3339 upper bound on occurred_at (recorded_at for workflow entries without one). Chain activity whose occurrence time is unknown is always included.

ThroughQueryRequired.name: through
ThroughQueryRequired.description: Exclusive RFC3339 end of the performance period; must be after from.

To.name: to
To.description: Exclusive RFC3339 window end, at most 24 hours after from. Omit from and to together for the server default.

taker_signature.description: Your EIP-712 signature over the quote's `signing` terms: `entry` as `TakerAccept`, or `sell_back` as `SellBack` (its digest is `quote_id`).

AcceptQuoteCommand.description: The taker's accept of the quote in the path. The `Idempotency-Key` header becomes the `acceptance_id`. For an entry, any part of the stake your free vault cash does not cover comes from your account wallet, through its USDC approval to WalletAccept (`POST /v1/me/wallet-approval`): approve once and each entry draws what it needs. Without an approval and wallet USDC that cover the shortfall, the trade fails with `reason` `INSUFFICIENT_APPROVAL` or `INSUFFICIENT_WALLET_USDC`. A scoped key draws the wallet only with `funding:deposit`.

status.description: `PENDING_CONFIRM`: waiting for the maker. `ACCEPTED`: the maker confirmed and the trade is queued as `operation_id`. `FILLED`: the trade committed on chain. `FAILED`: it reverted or expired unexecuted (see `reason`). `DECLINED`: the maker declined. `TIMED_OUT`: the maker did not answer in its two seconds. `CANCELLED`: the quote or RFQ went away first.

acceptance_id.description: The accept's `Idempotency-Key`: which of your accepts took the quote.

quote_id.description: The accepted quote. A quote has at most one acceptance.

confirm_within_ms.description: While `PENDING_CONFIRM`: milliseconds the maker had left to answer when the venue read the acceptance. Read it again once they pass.

operation_id.description: The on-chain operation that executes the trade; present once status is `ACCEPTED`, `FILLED` or `FAILED`.

reason.description: Why a `FAILED` acceptance funded from the wallet failed, when the venue can tell: the wallet's approval (`INSUFFICIENT_APPROVAL`) or USDC (`INSUFFICIENT_WALLET_USDC`) fell short.

Acceptance.description: The one record of a taker accepting a quote. For an entry, the position it opens has the accepted `quote_id` as its `position_id`.

status.description: Status after the maker answered or its two seconds passed, as `Acceptance` names it; never `PENDING_CONFIRM`.

operation_id.description: The on-chain operation that executes the trade, once status is `ACCEPTED`, `FILLED` or `FAILED`.

reason.description: Why a `FAILED` wallet-funded acceptance failed, when the venue can tell.

AcceptanceResult.description: The accept response: the acceptance after the maker answered or its two seconds passed. For an entry, the position's `position_id` is the accepted `quote_id`.

kind.description: The account kind: `PARTICIPANT` for a personal account.
The account kind: `MAKER` for a maker vault.

id.description: The on-chain maker ID, as a decimal string.

chain_id.description: The HyperEVM chain of the maker's vault: 999 mainnet, 998 testnet.

vault_address.description: The Totalis vault contract the maker is registered in.

kind.description: The account kind: `OPERATOR`, never issued.

Account.description: The one account a key acts for: a personal account or a maker vault. A key never spans accounts.

AccountValue.description: What the account holds at Totalis at one HyperEVM block, in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC): wallet USDC, its cash in the vault and in vaults running off, what it paid for its open positions, and the profit it can still claim, net of the fee. Every amount is read from the chain at block_number. HyperCore balances are not included; read them from Hyperliquid.

freshness.description: CURRENT when every amount was read at block_number; UNKNOWN when the chain could not be read, or the projection did not reach that block in time, and every amount is null. Read again later.

amount.description: The account's value: wallet_usdc + vault_cash + run_off_cash + open_cost + claimable_profit. Null unless freshness is CURRENT.

block_number.description: The HyperEVM block every amount was read at. Null unless freshness is CURRENT.

wallet_usdc.description: USDC in the account's wallet on HyperEVM, including any already committed to a Totalis withdrawal or stake that has not landed. Null unless freshness is CURRENT.

vault_cash.description: All the account's cash in the vault, including any held for an operation that has not landed, so it can exceed GET /v1/me/balances' free vault cash. Null unless freshness is CURRENT.

run_off_cash.description: The account's cash in vaults running off, all together; GET /v1/me/balances lists it per vault. Null unless freshness is CURRENT.

open_positions.description: How many positions the account holds that have not settled: OPEN and AWAITING_SETTLEMENT in GET /v1/me/positions. Null unless freshness is CURRENT.

open_cost.description: What the account paid for those positions: the sum of their acquisition_cost. Null unless freshness is CURRENT.

claimable_profit.description: What claiming every SETTLED_UNCLAIMED position would pay the account: each one's unclaimed_profit minus floor(unclaimed_profit * fee_bps / 10000). Null unless freshness is CURRENT.

checkpoint.description: The vault projection the read used to find the account's positions. When freshness is CURRENT it has reached block_number.

action.description: Action this decision covers: MAKER_WITHDRAW or MAKER_QUOTE.

route.description: Funding route the decision covers, e.g. MAKER_VAULT.

available.description: Amount available for this action and route in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC); null with blockers when unavailable.

blockers.description: Machine-readable codes blocking the action, e.g. MAKER_WITHDRAW_PENDING or RECONCILIATION_MISMATCH; at least one when available is null.

activity_id.description: Stable activity identifier (64 lowercase hex characters), unchanged across revisions and replays.

revision.description: Revision of this activity view, as a decimal string; increases when the activity is revised.

sequence.description: Commit-visible publication sequence of the activity's vault, as a decimal string. Lists order each vault's activity by sequence, then activity_id, descending; an account that has activity in more than one vault (after a vault redeploy) gets them merged, most recently recorded first.

kind.description: Business type of the activity, e.g. DEPOSIT, ACCEPT, SETTLEMENT, CLAIM, or CORRECTION for a reorg reversal.

status.description: PENDING: in progress; UNKNOWN: outcome not yet known; COMMITTED: final at its source; FAILED or REVERTED: took no effect and moves no committed cash; CORRECTED: a correction entry reversing superseded activity.

occurred_at.description: RFC3339 evidence time; for workflow entries, the operation's creation time, which later revisions keep. Null when the occurrence time is uncertain, such as an order with no retained placement time.

recorded_at.description: RFC3339 time the activity was recorded (ingest order).

operation_ids.description: Totalis operation IDs linked to the activity; empty when none.

position_ids.description: Position IDs (bytes32 hex) the activity concerns; empty when none.

supersedes.description: Activity IDs this correction reverses; empty unless kind is CORRECTION.

transaction_hashes.description: HyperEVM transactions that back the activity, in evidence order; empty for HyperCore and venue-only records.

effects.description: Balance effects for the scoped subject, each in its own asset; empty only for ORDER and POSITION_TRANSFER, which move no cash.

fill.description: Trade details for FILL, CONVERSION and CREDIT; null for every other kind and for entries recorded before trade details were retained. A CREDIT is an outcome settlement: it sells all size shares of side at price, what one share of that side paid at settlement, so the gross payout is size times price before the fee effect.

counterparty.description: Address of the other party when known, such as a deposit's payer; null otherwise.

description_code.description: Machine-readable display code, e.g. DEPOSIT, WALLET_VAULT_TRANSFER, MAKER_WITHDRAW_REQUESTED or REORG_REVERSAL; defaults to the kind.

direction.description: A settlement credit sells its shares.

price.description: What one share of the side paid at settlement, from 0 to 1.

context.description: Freshness of this read: the oldest source observation and one freshness for every amount in the response.

items.description: Activities on this page, ordered by sequence, then activity_id, descending, within each vault; several vaults' activities are merged, most recently recorded first.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, bound to this response's snapshot; null on the last page. Send it back unchanged as cursor.

has_more.description: True when another page exists; true exactly when next_cursor is non-null.

asset_id.description: Stable asset identifier. HyperEVM tokens use CAIP-19 `eip155:<chain_id>/erc20:<lowercase address>`; HyperCore spot tokens use `hypercore:<mainnet|testnet>/token:<spotMeta tokenId>`.

symbol.description: Display symbol, e.g. USDC or HYPE. Not an identity (HyperEVM USDC and HyperCore USDC share it), but USDC is one dollar per whole unit on either chain.

decimals.description: Scale of the asset's atomic unit: 6 for HyperEVM USDC, 8 for HyperCore USDC and HYPE.

Asset.description: Asset an effect moves. Deltas of different assets are different units and are never summed or compared.

Balance.description: The account's spendable Totalis balance in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC): embedded wallet USDC plus free vault cash. HyperCore balances are read from Hyperliquid directly or through GET /v1/hypercore/portfolio.

amount.description: Spendable total in atomic USDC; null unless freshness is CURRENT. It is wallet USDC plus free vault cash minus the withdrawals and stake fundings in pending.wallet_reserved, floored at zero. A wallet deposit that has not committed stays in it.

freshness.description: The components' freshness: both come from one chain read, so both are CURRENT or both UNKNOWN. STALE is no longer returned.

components.description: The two parts of the balance: WALLET_USDC then VAULT_FREE.

pending.description: In-flight amounts behind the balance, in atomic USDC (6 decimals).

wallet_reserved.description: Wallet USDC already committed to open Totalis withdrawals, stake fundings and wallet deposits that have not committed, so not spendable from the wallet. Withdrawals and stake fundings are subtracted from amount; a wallet deposit only moves into the vault and is not.

vault_deposits.description: Deposits into the vault that are queued or in flight and not yet committed.

vault_withdrawals.description: Withdrawals out of the vault that are queued or in flight and not yet committed.

core_exits.description: Route 2 exits leaving the vault or awaiting their HyperCore credit, each counted once.

has_unknown_operations.description: True when one of the account's operations has status UNKNOWN, so balances may still change when it resolves.

checkpoint.description: The chain projection the pending operations come from. Wallet and vault amounts come from a latest read at or after this block, independent of the checkpoint's freshness.

run_off.description: The account's cash in vaults running off, one item per vault holding any or with a claim in flight, outside amount: it is owned but never spendable here. A Totalis embedded wallet's moves to its HyperCore spot balance automatically. Any other wallet claims it to its own wallet, part of Cash, with one Exit signed for that vault and sent with Create run-off claim; a sponsored claim must move at least 1 USDC (1000000), so offer it only when freshness is CURRENT, vault_free is at least that and claim is null. Smaller amounts stay in the vault. Empty when no vault is running off.

kind.description: WALLET_USDC: embedded wallet USDC on HyperEVM; VAULT_FREE: unreserved cash held for the account in the Totalis vault.

amount.description: Component amount in atomic USDC (6 decimals); null when the component could not be read (freshness UNKNOWN).

freshness.description: CURRENT when the chain read that gives wallet and vault at one block answered; UNKNOWN when it did not. STALE is no longer returned.

cancelled.description: How many of your open quotes this call cancelled.

pending.description: How many it left up because a taker's acceptance awaits your answer: confirm or decline each, or let it time out.

CancelledQuotes.description: The outcome of cancelling all of your open quotes.

kind.description: RFQ kind; CASHOUT asks makers to quote the cash-out of an existing position.

taker.description: The position's owner, who signs to accept a quote.

maker_id.description: On-chain maker ID of the maker that originally underwrote the position.

net_stake.description: The position's stake after the taker fee, in atomic USDC (6 decimals): tickets(position_id).stake, which the vault fixes when the position opens.

payout.description: What the position pays if every leg wins, in atomic USDC (6 decimals): tickets(position_id).payout, which the vault fixes when the position opens.

status.description: OPEN collects cash-out quotes until expires_at; EXPIRED means that window passed without an accepted quote; CANCELLED means the owner cancelled it; ACCEPTED means a quote was accepted and confirmed; FAILED means the accepted sell-back failed on chain (see reason); DECLINED means every maker that could answer declined to quote it before expires_at.

reason.description: Why a FAILED RFQ ended: the accept transaction reverted, or it expired unexecuted. Present only when status is FAILED.

created_at.description: When the RFQ was durably created, RFC3339 UTC.

expires_at.description: When quote collection ends at the latest. A cash-out RFQ the owner opened runs up to an hour and closes sooner when the owner accepts, cancels or goes quiet (about two minutes after their last stream disconnects), or once a leg of its position settles (`RFQ_CANCELLED`). A created quote stays acceptable until its own expiry; the venue re-mints a price-only bid while the RFQ is open.

legs.description: The position's legs in canonical order.

scale.description: What one whole unit is: 10^18 for a chance (NO is scale minus each YES value, its low the YES high), 10^6 for a mark.

reducer.description: The reduction this body was cut with: per bucket and known stretch, first, lowest, highest and last value at their real times, in time order, a value serving several roles once, the earliest on a tie. A stretch held from before a bucket starts at the bucket's start; a null ends one where it was recorded, and a null at the bucket's start leaves the held value out; a value equal to the one held is no change. A client continuing the partial bucket uses the same one; the backend's shared reducer fixture holds its cases.

valid_until.description: The first instant the same request gets another grid: a step from the ladder (an ALL window growing past it), or minute closes where it read second detail or back (a window whose first day of points is dropped, a rolling window reaching where the record's points begin). Read again then; the answer is never cached past it. Null when the grid never changes.

step.description: Bucket length in microseconds: bucket i is [from + i * step, from + (i + 1) * step), half open; the last ends at to, or at end when that comes first. On minute grids a minute's close is its last value in [minute, minute + 1 minute), so it belongs to the bucket holding that minute: the close of a minute ending on a bucket edge belongs to the bucket before the edge.

grid.description: The grid the server picked, about 240 buckets: under a minute from second detail, otherwise from minute closes.

through.description: Everything before it is final: the last recorded minute edge on minute grids (the close of the minute ending at it is final, in the bucket before it), the last recorded bucket edge on finer ones, or end. A point at or after it comes from the live lane.

entering.description: The value held at grid.from, null when unknown there. When through precedes grid.from it is the value held at through: the live lane's points from through to grid.from move it without drawing anything.

points.description: Every bucket before the one holding through, reduced: each known stretch's first, lowest, highest and last value, and a null where the line became unknown.

start.description: Start of the bucket holding through.

points.description: Its stretches already ended before through, reduced, with their nulls.

open.description: The stretch still open at through, null when the line is unknown there.

partial.description: The bucket holding through, as reduced over [start, through); null when through is past the window.

end.description: Where an ended line stops (the market's expiry or recorded settlement, the earlier, once passed; for a mark line, that of the market it was asked for): nothing at or after it is drawn. Between grid edges it cuts the last bucket to [its start, end). Null before. Until the settlement is recorded an end from the expiry may still move or go back to null when the expiry is revised (final false, cached as a live line); from the settlement on it is the earlier of the expiry in effect then and the settlement, and never moves. The chart read is the only source of a line's end: read again when the market stream shows the market expired, postponed or settled.

final.description: True once end can no longer move: the market's settlement recorded it. False while end is null, comes from the expiry alone, or belongs to a settlement recorded before Totalis kept its end (read from the catalog's expiry now, cached as a live line).

Chart.description: One chart line on the server's grid.

ChartMicros.description: An instant in Unix microseconds. A line has at most one point per microsecond, so (line, instant) names a point.

value.description: The value from each instant on, aligned with at.

ChartPoints.description: Points in time order as two aligned arrays. A value holds until the next point; a null holds unknown until the next known value.

ChartSeries.description: A chart line: `chance:<outcome_id>` is the outcome's YES chance (any id a HIP-4 asset can have, 0 to 419496729), `mark:<coin>` a perp's mark.

first.description: The stretch's first value in the bucket, at its start or when it became known.

low.description: Its lowest value, the earliest on a tie.

high.description: Its highest value, the earliest on a tie.

ChartStretch.description: The reducer's state of the bucket's open known stretch: merge later points into it the way the server reduces a bucket.

oneOf.description: The value as an integer of the line's scale.
Unknown from here: the source stopped proving it, the market was withdrawn, or the recorder restarted.

ChartValue.description: A line's value, or null where it became unknown.

value.description: The value as an integer of the line's scale.

ChartVertex.description: One recorded value at its real time.

block_number.description: Last HyperEVM block the vault projection has indexed; the read reflects chain state up to and including this block.

freshness.description: CURRENT when the projection is within 32 blocks of a chain head observed in the last two minutes; STALE when it lags, so figures may be behind.

maker_id.description: Maker whose collateral requirement the job reduces.

status.description: QUEUED: waiting until the maker is eligible for a reduction; SOLVING: computing the requirement; NO_IMPROVEMENT: no lower requirement found, nothing to submit; DURABLE: certificate signed and ATTEST operation stored; FAILED: ended without a certificate.

snapshot_block.description: HyperEVM block of the maker's open-book snapshot; null until the snapshot is taken.

catalog_generation.description: Market-catalog generation the snapshot is bound to; null until the snapshot is taken.

gross0.description: Gross collateral requirement of the snapshot book in atomic USDC (6 decimals); null until the snapshot is taken.

risk0.description: Proven worst-case requirement of the snapshot book in atomic USDC (6 decimals); null until solved.

turnover0.description: Maker's settled turnover at the snapshot in atomic USDC (6 decimals), as signed into the certificate; null until the snapshot is taken.

nonce.description: Attestor nonce signed into the certificate; null without a certificate.

expiry.description: Certificate expiry in Unix seconds, two minutes after signing; null without a certificate.

digest.description: EIP-712 Attestation digest the attestor signed; null without a certificate.

operation_id.description: Maker-owned ATTEST operation that carries the certificate on chain; null without a certificate.

operation_status.description: Current status of the ATTEST operation; null without one.

transaction.description: Exact zero-value call for the maker to sign with its own gas account and submit through the self-funded transaction endpoint; null unless the operation is DURABLE and the certificate unexpired.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason the job failed, e.g. COOLDOWN_CHANGED; null otherwise.

next_eligible_at.description: Earliest RFC 3339 UTC time the maker's next reduction can land on chain; the job stays QUEUED until then.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC time the job was created.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC time the job last changed.

status.description: QUEUED: waiting until the maker is eligible for a reduction; SOLVING: computing the requirement; NO_IMPROVEMENT: no lower requirement found, nothing to submit; DURABLE: certificate signed and ATTEST operation stored; FAILED: ended without a certificate.

next_eligible_at.description: Earliest RFC 3339 UTC time the maker's next reduction can land on chain; the job stays QUEUED until then.

status_url.description: Relative path to poll for this job's status.

status.description: OPEN: an RFQ may include this market as a leg.
CLOSED: an RFQ that includes this market is refused; reason says why.

reason.description: EXCLUDED: Totalis keeps this market out of Combos. UNLISTED_DEPLOYER: its deployer is not one Totalis lists. OUTSIDE_WINDOW: its event is unknown or more than 7 days away, or the time its event starts or its result can be known is unknown. EVENT_PASSED: its event has started or its result can be known: the earliest of its observation time (a price market), its scheduled event (a game's start, a policy rate's decision) and its resolution backstop has passed, so makers refuse it.

opens_at.description: When the market enters the 7-day window, in Unix seconds: its best-known event time minus 7 days. Set only for OUTSIDE_WINDOW with a known event time before the window opens; approximate.

outcome_id.description: HIP-4 outcome ID the leg is on, as a decimal string. The signed Leg encodes it as uint32.

side.description: Outcome side the leg backs. The signed Leg encodes YES as 0 and NO as 1.

CommonLeg.description: One (outcome, side) pair, as markets and positions name it.

decision.description: Confirm and sign the accepted terms; the trade executes.

maker_signature.description: Your quote signer's EIP-712 signature over the accepted terms: `entry` as `Quote`, `sell_back` as `SellBack`. Your capital stays reserved for as long as this signature can execute.

decision.description: Decline the accepted terms. Nothing executes and the quote leaves the RFQ.

ConfirmQuoteCommand.description: Your answer to the acceptance, before its `deadline`, two seconds after the accept: `CONFIRM` with your signature, or `DECLINE`. Send no `Idempotency-Key`: the quote identifies its one acceptance.

status.description: The acceptance's status after your answer.

operation_id.description: The on-chain operation that executes the trade, once status is `ACCEPTED`, `FILLED` or `FAILED`.

title.description: Rendered display title; null when the template is unknown or the description does not fit it.

rules.description: Rendered resolution rules; the native description for a free-form market, null when the template is unknown or the description does not fit it.

exit_id.description: The exit ID: the Idempotency-Key it was created with.

status.description: Where the exit is; see the state values.

purpose.description: The purpose the exit was sent with; null for an ABANDONED tombstone.

amount.description: Atomic USDC (6 decimals) the Exit moves; null for an ABANDONED tombstone.

activation_fee_accepted.description: True only for an exit admitted to create a missing HyperCore account. Its Core credit is the full amount less a 1 USDC activation fee, or the full amount if the account was created first by someone else.

event_id.description: Identifier of the HyperCore ledger credit linked to this exit.

credit.description: The HyperCore spot credit the exit produced, or null until it is linked (status CREDITED).

CoreExitCommand.description: The account wallet's signed EIP-712 vault Exit that moves free vault cash to the account's HyperCore spot balance through the CoreExit router; Totalis relays it and pays the gas. The credential names the account: the Exit's account is the credential's account wallet, the vault account the cash leaves and the HyperCore account it reaches, and its to is deployment.router_address, so the body carries only the signed terms and the purpose.

amount.description: Atomic USDC (6 decimals) to move; at most the account's free vault cash. An account whose wallet is not a Totalis embedded wallet moves at least 1 USDC (1000000).

expiry.description: Exit expiry in Unix seconds, in the future and at most deployment.maximum_life_seconds ahead.

salt.description: Caller-chosen uint256 as a decimal string that makes the signed Exit unique.

signature.description: Signature by the account wallet over the EIP-712 Exit(account,to,amount,expiry,salt) digest, with account the credential's account wallet and to deployment.router_address; ECDSA or ERC-1271 contract signature bytes.

purpose.description: Why the cash moves: ORDER before a HyperCore order, WITHDRAW before a HyperCore withdrawal, SWEEP for a background move. A label only, except that SWEEP never accepts the activation fee.

activation_fee_accepted.description: Omitted means false. The user accepted that this exit creates their HyperCore account and that Hyperliquid takes a one-time 1 USDC activation fee from it. Required when the account does not exist yet; ignored when it does. Never accepted for SWEEP, and the exit must then move at least 2 USDC (2000000).

network.description: Hyperliquid network the router runs on.

chain_id.description: HyperEVM chain ID, as a decimal string: 999 mainnet, 998 testnet.

vault_address.description: The vault that verifies the Exit; its EIP-712 verifying contract.

router_address.description: The Exit's to: sign the Exit to this address. The body does not send it.

maximum_life_seconds.description: The furthest ahead, in seconds from now, an Exit expiry may be.

deployment.description: Where to sign Exits, or null when Core exits are off and POST /v1/core-exits returns CORE_EXIT_UNAVAILABLE.

exits.description: The account's unresolved exits from the active vault, to resume after a reload.

CoreExitState.description: ATTEMPT_FAILED is not terminal: the signed Exit can still execute until expiry, and a consumed digest is completed by a recovery relay. SENT is final on HyperEVM and waits for the Core credit without a timeout. RECOVERED means the account's signed router recover() returned the cash to an EVM recipient.

label.description: Your name for the key, 1 to 80 characters.

scopes.description: Permissions the key holds; each must apply to the account, as the capabilities route lists. Send `scopes` or `preset`, not both.

preset.description: A documented scope set instead of `scopes`. The owner signs, and the key holds, the scopes it expands to.

expires_in_days.description: Lifetime in days, 1 to 90, or 0 for no expiry; 30 when omitted.

proof.description: The account owner's signature over the challenge for exactly this request without `proof`.

CreateKeyRequest.description: The same shape for a personal account and a maker. proof is the owner's signature over the issue_key challenge for exactly this request without proof.

payout.description: Gross amount the position pays if every leg wins, in atomic USDC (6 decimals), before the profit fee. It must exceed the RFQ's stake. The venue fills in every other term: the RFQ's legs, stake and taker, the vault's current fees, your maker, a salt and an expiry. It keeps the quote takeable, renewing the expiry and salt and so its `quote_id`, until the RFQ closes or you replace or cancel it. Entry RFQs only.

price.description: What your maker vault pays the owner to close the position, in atomic USDC (6 decimals). The venue fills in every other sell-back term: the RFQ's position, owner and leg_state, a salt and an expiry that outlasts the RFQ, so the bid stays takeable until the RFQ closes or you replace or cancel it. Cash-out RFQs only, from the maker that backs the position.

CreateQuoteCommand.description: Your quote on the RFQ, which replaces your live quote there: `payout` on an entry RFQ, `price` on a cash-out RFQ, which only the maker that backs the position may quote. The venue fills in every other term.

stake.description: Stake in atomic USDC (6 decimals), before taker fees; must be positive. Quotes carry the same stake.

legs.description: 1 to 5 legs in strictly increasing outcome_id order, at most one per native question. Every leg's market must have eligibility ENABLED and combo OPEN, and a chance on each side.

builder_code.description: Optional partner builder code. It credits the partner whose app sent this RFQ with its revenue share and adds nothing to what you pay. An account the partner admitted gets its partner's code without sending one, and a code it sends must be that partner's. From any other account the code counts only when the request comes from the code's registered browser origin, so an API-key or server request from such an account cannot send one.

CreateRfqCommand.description: The entry RFQ to open: new legs and a stake, whose taker is the caller's account wallet. To sell a position you already hold, use `POST /v1/me/positions/{position_id}/cashout` instead.

rotated_from.description: Always null for a created key.

kind.description: Scheduled start, scheduled decision, or deadline named by the source rules.

at.description: When the event happens, in Unix seconds.

name.description: Display name: Hyperliquid for its own markets, the listed deployer's name, or null for a deployer Totalis does not list.

address.description: Deployer address, lowercase hex; null for Hyperliquid's own markets.

chain_id.description: EVM chain ID of the deployment and the EIP-712 domain chainId, as a decimal string: 999 on HyperEVM mainnet, 998 on testnet.

vault_address.description: Canonical Totalis vault contract of this deployment, and the EIP-712 domain verifyingContract of every Totalis signature.

source_revision.description: Git commit, 40 lowercase hex characters, of the deployed contract source.

audit_status.description: PRE_AUDIT until the deployment's contracts complete an external audit, then AUDITED.

fee_bps.description: The vault's current profit fee in basis points, charged at claim on the winning profit (payout minus net stake). Every quote must carry exactly this fee_bps to be accepted. Null until the venue has recorded the vault's settings.

taker_fee_bps.description: The vault's current entry fee in basis points, taken from the stake at accept. Every quote must carry exactly this taker_fee_bps to be accepted. Null until the venue has recorded the vault's settings.

usdc.description: The canonical USDC token the vault holds, and the domain its EIP-3009 authorizations (deposit funding and withdrawal payouts) are signed under.

address.description: USDC token contract on this chain; approve the vault on it before a maker deposit.

eip712_domain.description: EIP-712 domain for USDC ReceiveWithAuthorization and TransferWithAuthorization signatures.

name.description: Domain name of the USDC token; always USDC.

version.description: Domain version of the USDC token; always 2.

chain_id.description: Domain chain ID as a decimal string; equals the deployment chain_id.

Deployment.description: The canonical contract deployment clients sign against. Totalis structs are signed under the TotalisParlay v1 domain with chainId chain_id and verifyingContract vault_address.

operation_id.description: ID of the queued deposit operation; follow it with GET /v1/me/operations/{operation_id}.

status.description: Always DURABLE: the deposit is recorded and queued, not yet executed on chain.

amount.description: Deposit amount in atomic USDC (6 decimals), the signed authorization `value`.

DepositCommand.description: The account wallet's signed EIP-3009 ReceiveWithAuthorization moving USDC into the vault; Totalis relays it and pays gas. The credential names the account: its account wallet both pays and is credited, so the body carries only the signed terms.

amount.description: Deposit amount in atomic USDC (6 decimals); at least "100000" (0.10 USDC) from a Privy login wallet, embedded or external, and "1000000" (1 USDC) from any other, and no more than the wallet's USDC not already committed to other pending work.

valid_after.description: EIP-3009 validAfter in Unix seconds; must not be in the future.

valid_before.description: EIP-3009 validBefore in Unix seconds; must be at least 5 seconds ahead and at most 900 seconds after `valid_after`.

salt.description: Random 32 bytes; the EIP-3009 nonce is `keccak256(abi.encode(vault, chainId, wallet, salt, wallet))`, where wallet is the caller's account wallet.

authorization_signature.description: 65-byte ECDSA signature by the account wallet over the USDC ReceiveWithAuthorization message, with the vault as payee.

title.description: Display title of the question, standalone market or price series.

status.description: Lifecycle of the item: ACTIVE, CLOSED or UNSUPPORTED; for a question or price series, ACTIVE when any of its markets is active.

category.description: Display category, or null when the item is not mapped to one.

subcategory.description: Display subcategory slug within the category; null when unmapped or not subdivided.

items.description: Matching questions and standalone markets, best match first.

catalog_generation.description: Catalog generation every item in this page was read from. Discovery without a browse contract continues by native ID when a new generation is published, so a later page can name a newer generation; a search cursor stays bound to its generation and returns STALE_CURSOR after one, and a browse-contract cursor keeps reading the publication it came from while that is retained (five minutes), then returns STALE_CURSOR.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor with the same query to read the next page; null when there are no more pages.

id.description: Item ID, question: followed by the native question ID.

kind.description: QUESTION: a multi-outcome question.

markets.description: The question's markets in the current catalog.

id.description: Item ID, market: followed by the outcome ID.

kind.description: STANDALONE: a single binary market with no question.

native_question_id.description: Always null for a standalone market.

asset.description: Asset the delta is denominated in.

bucket.description: Balance lane the delta applies to: WALLET, CORE_SPOT, CORE_MARGIN, VAULT_USER (the account's vault balance), MAKER_VAULT, STAKE_ESCROW, PAYABLE, REQUIREMENT, RESERVATION, IN_TRANSIT, REALIZED_PNL or FEE.

delta.description: Signed change to the bucket in atomic units of asset, e.g. "1000000" = 1 USDC on HyperEVM (6 decimals) and "100000000" = 1 USDC on HyperCore (8 decimals). Lane deltas are not summable income.

classification.description: Economic meaning: EXTERNAL_CAPITAL (deposit or withdrawal across the subject boundary), INTERNAL_TRANSFER (move between the subject's own lanes), TRADE, FEE, HOLD (reservation) or CORRECTION (reorg reversal).

status.description: DISABLED: Totalis does not currently accept new positions on this market; reason says why.

reason.description: Why new positions are refused. UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION, UNSUPPORTED_QUOTE_ASSET and IDENTITY_CONFLICT are permanent support failures; MARKET_NOT_ACTIVE means the native market is no longer live; NATIVE_STATE_UNAVAILABLE, NATIVE_STATE_STALE, REFERENCE_UNAVAILABLE, REFERENCE_STALE and SOURCE_GENERATION_MISMATCH are temporary data outages; FINANCIAL_PROFILE_DISABLED means trading is switched off in this environment; SOURCE_UNQUALIFIED marks cached catalog copies that carry no live eligibility.

status.description: ENABLED: Totalis currently accepts new positions on this market.

kind.description: Always `ENTRY`: the accepted quote opens a new position.

deadline.description: Confirm before this instant, an RFC3339 UTC timestamp. A later answer cannot reopen the acceptance.

entry.description: Accepted entry terms; sign them as `Quote`.

EntryMakerAcceptance.description: A taker's accept of your entry quote.
EntryMakerAcceptance.title: Entry acceptance

quote_id.description: Quote ID. Accept it with `POST /v1/quotes/{quote_id}/accept`; it becomes the position's `position_id`.

kind.description: Always `ENTRY`: the quote opens a new position.

sequence.description: Venue-wide publication sequence number; a higher value was created later.

payout.description: What the position pays if every leg wins, in atomic USDC (6 decimals), before the profit fee.

entry.description: The entry terms the taker signs as the EIP-712 `TakerAccept` struct to accept.

signing.description: What the taker signs to accept. The SDK signs it for you.

EntryQuote.description: A maker's offer to open a position on an entry RFQ.
EntryQuote.title: Entry quote

kind.description: RFQ kind; ENTRY asks makers to quote a new position.

taker.description: Wallet that signs the accept and will own the position.

stake.description: Stake in atomic USDC (6 decimals), before taker fees.

net_stake.description: What the vault backs if a quote is accepted, in atomic USDC (6 decimals): stake - floor(stake * taker_fee_bps / 10000), with the taker_fee_bps every quote must carry (the vault's current taker fee). Price the position on this; quotes still sign the gross stake. Absent while the taker fee is unknown.

status.description: OPEN collects quotes until expires_at; EXPIRED means that window passed without an accepted quote; CANCELLED means the owner cancelled it; ACCEPTED means a quote was accepted and confirmed; FAILED means the accepted trade failed on chain (see reason); DECLINED means every maker that could answer declined to quote it before expires_at.

reason.description: Why a FAILED RFQ ended: the accept transaction reverted (REVERTED), it expired unexecuted (EXPIRED_UNEXECUTED), or the taker's Cash did not cover the stake when it was to execute (INSUFFICIENT_CASH). The accept's operation then has `reason` INSUFFICIENT_CASH. Present only when status is FAILED.

created_at.description: When the RFQ was durably created, RFC3339 UTC.

expires_at.description: When quote collection ends at the latest. An RFQ the taker opened runs up to an hour and closes sooner when the taker accepts, cancels or goes quiet: about two minutes after their last stream disconnects (`RFQ_CANCELLED`). One the venue opened for the taker, such as a copied trade, ends 20 seconds after creation.

legs.description: Requested legs in strictly increasing outcome_id order.

error.description: The one error this request failed with.

ErrorCode.description: Stable HTTP error code. Each code has one HTTP status and one retry value.

code.description: Stable registered code; branch on this, not on message or status.

field_violations.description: Each invalid input by JSON pointer; empty when the error is not about a specific input.

request_id.description: UUIDv7 of this request, also returned in the X-Request-ID header. Quote it when reporting a problem.

retry.description: What the caller should do next; fixed by the registry for each code.

FactorNumerator.description: Native result numerator in the inclusive range zero through Q = 100000000.

code.description: REQUIRED: the input is missing. INVALID: it is present but malformed or out of range. UNEXPECTED: the input is not accepted here.

field.description: JSON pointer into the body, or into the query parameters as one flat object for requests without a body, for example /legs/0/stake or /limit.

outcome_id.description: HIP-4 outcome ID traded, as a decimal string.

side.description: Outcome side traded, YES or NO.

direction.description: BUY or SELL of side, as Hyperliquid reported it; always SELL for a settlement credit.

size.description: Shares filled, as an exact decimal string with no trailing zeros.

price.description: Price per share in USDC, as an exact decimal string with no trailing zeros; 0 is possible for a conversion leg or a losing settlement.

oid.description: Hyperliquid order ID, as a decimal string.

tid.description: Hyperliquid trade ID, as a decimal string.

Fill.description: The traded leg of a HyperCore fill, conversion or settlement credit. Cash and fees stay in effects.

sport.description: Sport as the first member names it, trimmed.

scheduled_start.description: Scheduled start every member shares, RFC 3339 UTC.

participants.description: The two participants in the first member's order, trimmed. Other members may list them the other way round; each keeps its own orientation and sides.

winner_outcome_ids.description: Members that pick the contest winner (sportsContestWinner), in market order.

spread_outcome_ids.description: Members on participantA's points spread (sportsSpread), in market order.

total_outcome_ids.description: Members on the combined total (sportsTotal), in market order.

GameStream.description: A live channel on a provider's player, which plays whatever the channel has on air.

provider.description: The player the channel plays on.

channel.description: The channel's login on the provider, such as pgl_cs2.

GenesisEarnedAt.description: When the account earned the Genesis Account badge. Others see it only while the account's public profile is on.

minute.description: Inclusive UTC start of the one-minute bucket, RFC 3339; the clock is given by the response's bucket_time.

open.description: First price in the bucket, at the response's scale.

high.description: Highest price in the bucket, at the response's scale.

low.description: Lowest price in the bucket, at the response's scale.

close.description: Last price in the bucket, at the response's scale.

volume.description: Executed base size in the bucket, divided by the response's volume_scale for contracts; null for reference-price bars.

trade_count.description: Number of trades in the bucket; null for reference-price bars.

outcome_id.description: Hyperliquid outcome ID of the market.

source.description: Hyperliquid feed whose data is missing.

catalog_generation.description: Catalog generation in effect when the gap was recorded.

feed_generation.description: Price feed generation that recorded the gap.

from.description: Inclusive start of the missing interval, RFC 3339 UTC, clipped to the requested window.

to.description: Exclusive end of the missing interval, RFC 3339 UTC, clipped to the requested window.

reason.description: Why data is missing: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE when the feed was down, SPOOL_FULL when local buffering overflowed, NO_OBSERVATION, CORRUPT_SEGMENT or UPLOAD_FAILED for other recording losses.

IntegerValue.description: Nonnegative integer value paired with an explicit positive scale.

status.description: Always `ACTIVE` for a new key.

last_used_at.description: Always null for a new key.

revoked_at.description: Always null for a new key.

overlap_until.description: Always null for a new key.

secret.description: The `ttk_` secret, shown only in this response; a retry of the same request answers `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`, so store it now.

KeyCapabilities.description: Advisory, no-store snapshot of the scopes a new key for this account may hold and the signer whose signature issues it. Scope dependencies still apply. Issuance revalidates current authority and consumes the signer's proof; discovery is never an authorization lease.

account.description: The account a new key would act for.

environment.description: The deployment a new key would work in.

signer.description: The address that signs issuance: the account wallet for a personal account, the controller for a maker.

scopes.description: Scopes a new key for this account may hold now.

signer.description: The address that must sign: the account wallet for a personal account, the controller for a maker.

message.description: The EIP-4361 message to sign with `personal_sign`, exactly as returned; check its URI, account, action and key before signing.

expires_at.description: When the challenge stops being accepted, 5 minutes after issue.

KeyChallenge.description: An EIP-4361 (SIWE) message with purpose=issue_key. Its resources bind the environment, vault, account, owner version (makers), action, key (rotation) and the request digest.

request.description: The exact create request, without `proof`, that the owner signs.
The exact rotation request, without `proof`, that the owner signs.

KeyExpiryDays.description: 0 means Forever (no expiry); 1–90 sets a finite lifetime in days. Omission defaults to 30.

items.description: Keys of the account, oldest first, revoked and expired ones included.

next_cursor.description: Send as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

id.description: Key ID; the secret embeds it, and the key routes take it as `key_id`.

account.description: The one account the key acts for.

environment.description: The deployment the key works in; a key never works in another.

label.description: Your name for the key, 1 to 80 characters.

scopes.description: Permissions the key holds; each operation lists the scopes it requires.

status.description: `ACTIVE`; `ROTATING` once a rotation replaced it, until `overlap_until`; `EXPIRED` past its deadline; or `REVOKED`.

expires_at.description: Null means no scheduled expiry. Revocation, overlap deadlines and current authority still apply.

last_used_at.description: When the key last authenticated a request, or null if never.

revoked_at.description: When the key was revoked, or null.

rotated_from.description: The key this one replaced in a rotation, or null for a newly created key.

overlap_until.description: While `ROTATING`, when this replaced key stops working; otherwise null.

kind.description: The account kind: `PARTICIPANT` for a personal account.

account.description: Applies when the key's account is of this kind.

scopes.description: Scopes that never apply to this account kind are refused.

kind.description: The account kind: `MAKER` for a maker vault.

account.description: Applies when the key's account is of this kind.

scopes.description: Scopes that never apply to this account kind are refused.

kind.description: The account kind: `OPERATOR`, never issued.

account.description: Applies when the key's account is of this kind.

status.description: Applies to a revoked key.

revoked_at.description: Null unless the key is revoked.

status.description: Applies to a key being replaced.

overlap_until.description: Set while the key is being replaced.

status.description: Applies to an active key.

KeyPreset.description: A documented scope set. `TAKER`, for a personal key: identity:read, account:read, account:stream, replay:read, rfq:write, quote:read, quote:accept, position:cashout, sponsorship:use, funding:deposit and funding:withdraw. `MAKER`, for a maker key, the quoting bot's: rfq:read, quote:read, quote:write, replay:read and vault:read, none of which move vault money.

outcome_id.description: HIP-4 outcome ID of the leg, as a decimal string.

side.description: Outcome side the position holds, YES or NO.

status.description: RESOLVED: the outcome has a final result.

result_numerator.description: Selected-side result factor over result_denominator: 100000000 is a full win, 0 a loss, values between are fractional.

outcome_id.description: HIP-4 outcome ID of the leg, as a decimal string.

side.description: Outcome side the position holds, YES or NO.

status.description: UNRESOLVED: result still pending; UNAVAILABLE: historical result evidence is missing.

result_numerator.description: Null until the leg has a known result.

result_denominator.description: Null until the leg has a known result.

coin.description: The perp, as Hyperliquid names it: BTC, or a builder-deployed perp with its dex, xyz:SP500.

px.description: The perp's mark from Totalis's newest read of its own node, as the node gave it; null when that read did not answer it or Totalis has had no read for 3 seconds (the market stream's unavailable_after_ms): unknown, never an earlier mark.

observed_at.description: Node time at the start of the read that proved px, null exactly when px is: the mark held at some node instant of that read, which starts here and usually ends milliseconds later. The same instant as that read's from on the market stream's mark frame. Judge its age from here, never from when the answer arrived.

marks.description: Every perp a listed price market charts, by coin. A perp not listed is not read at all. Empty before the first read.

MakerAcceptance.description: A taker's accept of your quote, waiting for your confirm until `deadline`, told apart by `kind`. `QUOTE_ACCEPTED`, the maker snapshot's `acceptances` and List pending acceptances carry the same item. It never includes the taker's signature or `acceptance_id`.

acceptances.description: Acceptances of your quotes waiting for your confirm on this page, earliest deadline first. One answered or expired since the snapshot is left out; a new one arrives on the stream.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null when has_more is false.

has_more.description: True when another page follows; send next_cursor to read it.

MakerAcceptanceList.description: Acceptances a maker snapshot left out past its cap; the snapshot names this route in `truncated`. Items match the snapshot's `acceptances` and `QUOTE_ACCEPTED`.

maker_id.description: On-chain maker ID this access applies to, as a decimal string.

controller.description: Maker controller address the access was verified against.

controller_version.description: Maker controller epoch at verification, as a decimal string; a controller change invalidates access derived from an earlier epoch.

access_revision.description: Revision of the controller's wallet link, as a decimal string. It changes when the wallet is unlinked and relinked, which expires cursors bound to the old revision.

permissions.description: Read permissions held. They never authorize signing or spending.

context.description: Freshness of this read: the oldest source observation and one freshness for every amount in the response.

controller.description: Maker controller, from the same indexed vault row as the lanes.

signer.description: Maker signer (its quote signer) from the same indexed vault row as the lanes. The zero address means the maker was opened without one and cannot quote.

vault_gross.description: Maker vault lane V from the vault contract, including escrow and payables.

stake_escrow.description: Bettor net stakes escrowed in this maker's open positions (E).

payable_owed.description: Settled winnings owed to position holders and not yet claimed (P).

gross_open.description: Original open maker exposure G: payout minus net stake summed over open positions.

discount.description: Maker discount lane D from the vault contract, which offsets gross_open in the requirement.

requirement.description: Collateral requirement R = max(G - min(D, G), ceil(G * floor_bps / 10000)) under the pinned release; null when floor_bps is null or an input is null.

free_collateral.description: Collateral headroom F = max(V - E - P - R, 0). Not a guarantee of quote acceptance.

capital_net_of_senior_liabilities.description: Signed C = V - E - P. Excludes open-position valuation; not equity or NAV.

pending_commitments.description: Admission reservations H the venue holds for this maker that are not yet reflected on-chain; the sum of reservations.

free_after_pending.description: max(F - H, 0): free collateral after unreflected commitments. Not private bot capacity.

floor_bps.description: Requirement floor K in basis points from the pinned release; null when the on-chain comparison mismatches, which makes requirement UNAVAILABLE.

deployment_digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact pinned artifact that names this deployment's chain and vault: the release artifact on chain 999, the environment's deployment manifest on 998. A client compares it with its own pinned artifact to bind the read to its deployment.

actions.description: Decisions for MAKER_WITHDRAW and MAKER_QUOTE on the MAKER_VAULT route. MAKER_WITHDRAW is the amount a new withdrawal request may ask for: free_after_pending, so it never takes collateral from fills already admitted. The vault re-checks free collateral when the request executes after its delay; it is null with MAKER_WITHDRAW_PENDING while a request is live, or with a reconciliation blocker. MAKER_QUOTE is the most new quotes may promise: free_after_pending less a live v1 withdrawal request's amount, never below zero. Quotes reserve nothing, so it does not count the maker's other live quotes; if several are accepted at once, a confirm past it fails QUOTE_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED. Both are null with a reconciliation blocker while the vault read and venue records disagree.

reservations.description: Venue reservations on MAKER_VAULT that make up pending_commitments.

MakerCapital.description: Maker capital lanes and derived collateral, in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC). Amounts are null when unavailable; context.freshness says how fresh they are.

items.description: Keys of the account, oldest first.

kind.description: The account kind: `MAKER` for a maker vault.

account.description: The account the key acts for.

maker_id.description: Maker this withdrawal schedule belongs to.
