controller.description: Maker wallet: the only wallet that can withdraw (withdrawMaker on vault v1.1; requestMakerWithdraw, executeMakerWithdraw and cancelMakerWithdraw on vault v1). It sends each call itself and pays the gas in HYPE.

pending.description: The live v1 withdrawal request, or null when none is pending; always null on vault v1.1, which pays at once. A maker has at most one: a new request reverts until this one executes or is cancelled.

as_of_block.description: Last HyperEVM block the projection behind this read has processed.

freshness.description: CURRENT when the projection is caught up with the chain; STALE when it lags, so a recent request, execute or cancel may not show yet.

amount.description: Requested amount in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC).

destination.description: Address the vault pays on execute, fixed when the request was made.

ready_at.description: Earliest time executeMakerWithdraw can succeed: the request time plus the vault's withdrawal delay (24 hours on mainnet).

executable.description: True when blockers is empty: executeMakerWithdraw would succeed now on the state this read saw. The vault re-checks everything when it runs.

blockers.description: Why execute would revert now: WITHDRAW_NOT_READY before ready_at, VAULT_PAUSED while the vault is paused, MAKER_SHORT while the vault lane is below escrow plus payables, INSUFFICIENT_FREE while the amount exceeds free collateral. The request stays pending; cancel it to request a different amount.

outcome_id.description: Hyperliquid outcome ID of the market.

native_question_id.description: Hyperliquid question this market belongs to; null for a standalone market.

title.description: Display title derived from the market definition.

status.description: Native lifecycle: ACTIVE while the market is live on Hyperliquid, CLOSED once it is no longer live, UNSUPPORTED when Totalis does not support it.

result.description: Native result as last read from HyperEVM.

metadata_revision.description: Revision of this market's catalog metadata; it increases when the metadata changes.

eligibility.description: Whether Totalis currently accepts new positions on this market, with the reason when it does not.

combo.description: Whether a Combo may take this market as a leg, decided at read time. Independent of eligibility: a market can trade alone while Combos are closed to it.

deployer.description: Who deployed the market on Hyperliquid.

category.description: Display category, or null when the market is not mapped to one.

subcategory.description: Display subcategory slug within the category, for example btc; null when unmapped or not subdivided.

sides.description: The YES and NO sides, in that order.

dates.description: Display dates and the market class; null when the market has neither reviewed timing nor a market class. Never controls availability or settlement.

awaiting_result.description: For display only: whether the market's event is over while Hyperliquid has not recorded its result. true when a live scoreboard shows its game final (every winner, spread and total market of that game) or a price market's observation time has passed with its result unresolved; false when its event is known not to be over yet or its result is recorded; null or absent when unknown: other kinds of market, a game no scoreboard covers or reads now, or a native result that could not be read. It never closes trading, settles, or changes chance, mark, eligibility or Combo admission.

MarketDates.description: UTC instants from typed Hyperliquid template keywords, and the reviewed market class. event, result_by and resolves_after are display-only, null when already interpolated into the title. scheduled_event_at and observation_ends_at are always given when known; outside sports games, the earlier of them is when Combos close to the market. A market with neither (a deadline-only award or IPO market) closes at its resolution backstop, which the venue enforces at RFQ entry; it is not exposed here.

event.description: The scheduled event the market is about; null when unknown or already in the title.

result_by.description: Latest instant at which the source rules fix the result, in Unix seconds; null when unknown or already in the title.

resolves_after.description: Resolution cannot occur before this instant, in Unix seconds; not a settlement promise. Null when unknown or already in the title.

scheduled_event_at.description: Scheduled start or decision named by the source rules, in Unix seconds; null when the market has none.

observation_ends_at.description: End of the observation window named by the source rules, in Unix seconds; null when the market has none.

market_class.description: Reviewed market class, for example PRICE_BINARY, PRICE_TOUCH or SPORTS_TOURNAMENT; null when no reviewed rule classifies the market.

game.description: Present only when the contract=4 query parameter selects browse contract 4: the game this standalone market belongs to with up to 256 current members, or null when it has none, is its only current member or has more active members than 256. Absent otherwise.

estimated_live_until.description: Present only when the contract=4 query parameter selects browse contract 4: end of the in-play window of the market's matchup, as the browse card of its question, else of its game, else of the market as a standalone contest shows it. The window starts at the scheduled start (dates.scheduled_event_at; game.scheduled_start for a game) and lasts its league's reviewed usual game length, unless the live game feed shows the game in play (then at least 15 minutes past the read, extended until it ends) or over (then the moment it was first seen over, or the start if that was earlier). Never a trading cutoff, closure or settlement. Present before the contest starts. Null for anything else: tournaments, series, leagues without a reviewed length, or markets that disagree on the start. Absent otherwise.

scoreboard.description: Present only when the contract=4 query parameter selects browse contract 4: the game of the market's matchup (its question's, else its game's, else its own) as the live game feed last read it, for display only. Null when estimated_live_until is null, the feed does not cover or could not match the game, or its last reading of an unfinished game is stale. Absent otherwise.

catalog_generation.description: Catalog generation the market, question and metadata were read from.

market.description: The market with its current references, eligibility and result.

question.description: Parent question with all of its markets; null for a standalone market.

series_id.description: Key of the series this standalone market belongs to, the series_id of the series read; set even while it is the only listed member. A binaryPrice or priceTouch market carries it unless it is a round of a recurring template stream, which recurring_round describes instead; a companyIpoFirstDayMarketCap market only when the contract=4 query parameter selects browse contract 4. Null for every other market.

metadata.description: Display title and rules of the market, its sides and its parent question, read at the same catalog generation as market.

recurring_round.description: The recurring round the market belongs to, with its recorded neighbours: a native recurring round or a round of a template stream whose cadence recorded history proved. Null for a market outside a recurring series or a round whose recorded definition is withheld.

stats.description: This market's 24h volume and open interest; null until a current stats snapshot has a row for it.

updated_at.description: Latest change to the market's catalog record, native result or reference prices, RFC 3339 UTC.

volume_24h.description: Side 0 24h notional volume in atomic USDC (6 decimals).

open_interest.description: Mean circulating supply of the two sides, in atomic USDC (6 decimals).

MarketDetailStats.description: This market's row of the stats snapshot, refreshed about every minute from Hyperliquid asset contexts. Display data only; it never gates trading.

network.description: Hyperliquid network the outcomes are listed on.

imagery_publication.description: The imagery manifest publication every subject was resolved from. null while market-data holds no manifest: every picture that would name a subject is then null and `subjects` is empty, the Draw and Total glyphs still show, and the answer is never cached.

outcomes.description: Every asked outcome Totalis recorded, live or departed, ascending by outcome ID.

subjects.description: Each subject the outcomes' pictures name, once, by key.

not_recorded.description: Asked outcome IDs Totalis holds no definition of although it recorded a newer one, such as one no catalog listed and Hyperliquid has not settled yet: nothing names or pictures them. Ascending.

pending.description: Asked outcome IDs newer than every outcome Totalis recorded, such as one listed seconds ago: ask again shortly. An answer with any is never cached. Ascending.

items.description: One template object in Hyperliquid's own shape.

templates.description: The entries of Hyperliquid's info `outcomeTemplates` answer, unchanged, that these outcomes and their questions are instances of, from the current catalog generation's template list, ascending by `id`. A template Hyperliquid no longer lists is left out: name that outcome by `title`.

id.description: Item ID, the same ID as the discovery card.

catalog_generation.description: Catalog generation the game and its markets were read from, the detail's generation.

game.description: What the members share and their roles.

markets.description: Current members in game order with live state and prices: the requested market, every active member, then the newest inactive members up to 256.

outcome_id.description: Hyperliquid outcome ID of the market.

side.description: Market side every bar describes, YES or NO.

series_type.description: TRADE_OHLCV: bars are one-minute OHLCV of executed trade prices, with base-size volume. REFERENCE_PRICE_OHLC: bars are one-minute OHLC of indicative mid prices, falling back to the last trade, without volume. Minutes without observations have no bar and are never filled in.

source.description: Hyperliquid feed every bar in the response was built from.

quality.description: Price quality every bar in the response carries.

scale.description: Divisor for open, high, low and close of every bar and the anchor; null when there are neither. Currently 1000000000000000000 (18 decimals); a scale change starts a new page.

volume_scale.description: Divisor for volume of every bar and the anchor; null for reference-price history or when there are no bars.

from.description: Authoritative window start. It repeats the request, or the rolling 24-hour default when from and to are both omitted. Reuse these bounds for later pages.

to.description: Authoritative exclusive window end. It repeats the request, or the request time when from and to are both omitted. Reuse these bounds for later pages.

bucket_time.description: minute is the inclusive UTC bucket start on this clock; bucket end is exclusive one minute later. Only full closed buckets contained in [from,to) appear in bars.

closed_before.description: Exclusive bucket boundary, the earlier of to or server time rounded down to a minute. This is not a persistence or coverage watermark. Closed buckets can still be repaired.

anchor.description: Latest retained earlier full bucket within the 90-day online window for the selected source and side, last received before from. Its close is an observed price, not proof that the value held through from. Null when there is none or its scale differs from the bars.

bars.description: Closed one-minute bars in the window, ascending by minute.

gaps.description: Recorded data gaps overlapping the window; empty unless gaps were requested.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor with the same from and to to read the next page; null when there are no more bars.

has_more.description: True when more bars follow in the window.

volume.description: Executed base size in the bucket; always present for trade bars.

trade_count.description: Number of trades in the bucket; at least 1 for trade bars.

volume_scale.description: Divisor for volume; null only when there are no bars.

volume.description: Always null; reference-price bars carry no volume.

trade_count.description: Always null; reference-price bars carry no trade count.

source.description: Reference feed with missing data: HYPERLIQUID_L2_BOOK, HYPERLIQUID_BBO or HYPERLIQUID_ALL_MIDS.

volume_scale.description: Always null; reference-price bars carry no volume.

source.description: Reference feed; HYPERLIQUID_L2_BOOK in this branch.
Reference feed; HYPERLIQUID_BBO in this branch.
Reference feed; HYPERLIQUID_ALL_MIDS in this branch.

items.description: Markets on this page, ascending by outcome ID.

catalog_generation.description: Catalog generation every item in this page was read from. A cursor continues by native ID when a new generation is published, so a later page can name a newer generation than an earlier one.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor to read the next page; null when there are no more pages.

side.description: Which side of the binary market this entry describes, YES or NO.

coin.description: Hyperliquid coin name of this side, # followed by outcome_id times 10 plus the side index (0 for YES, 1 for NO).

reference.description: Current reference price of this side, or why none is available.

last_chance.description: For display only: the side's last real chance at the probability scale (10^18), set only while the market's awaiting_result is true and reference.chance is null. It is the newest evidence the chance rule holds, unclamped: the last book execution, or the last midpoint of a book at most 10% of scale wide. It needs a fresh, uncrossed book on this side; an empty book keeps it. YES and NO sum to scale. Null or absent otherwise. It is not a price, a value or a chance: never trade, value a position or pick a Combo leg with it.

id.description: Unique per taker order, token and block: height, Hyperliquid order ID, coin number and side letter (B buy, A sell). Merge by it.

market_side.description: The outcome token the taker's order traded, YES or NO, also where its fills took liquidity from the other token's book: selling YES into NO bids is a YES sale.

direction.description: BUY when the taker acquired market_side's token, SELL when it disposed of it. A chart of the YES price reads BUY NO as bearish.

shares.description: Exact sum of the order's filled shares on the token in this block.

avg_price.description: notional / shares rounded to 8 decimals, halves away from zero; display only, the exact numbers are notional and shares.

notional.description: Gross trade size in quote: exact sum of price × shares over the order's fills, before fees, the same for buys and sells.

quote.description: The asset notional and avg_price are in: the outcome's quote asset, as Hyperliquid names it on the fills (USDC for every outcome Totalis supports). Null when the fills do not name one.

height.description: HyperCore block height of the fills: the order executed in this block.

oid.description: Hyperliquid order ID of the taker's order.

taker.description: The taker's HyperCore address, lowercase, as public on Hyperliquid. Nothing else about the trader is attached.

MarketTakerOrder.description: One taker order's execution on one outcome token in one HyperCore block: every fill of the order that crossed the book in that block (dir Buy or Sell, crossed), summed exactly. Makers' sides, settlements, splits, merges and negations are never orders. A Hyperliquid order executes in the block that includes it, so an order is one event; a part that rests and is hit later is a maker fill and not repeated. Two orders of one trader in one block stay two.

Metric.description: Signed amount in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC); null when it could not be established, never zero in its place.

NextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when has_more is false.

kind.description: Operation type, named after the contract call: DEPOSIT_USER_AUTHORIZED, WITHDRAW_USER, ACCEPT, SETTLE, CLAIM, SELL_BACK, POSITION_TRANSFER, TOTALIS_PAYOUT, CORE_EXIT or ATTEST. Treat unlisted values as opaque.

amount.description: Atomic USDC (6 decimals): the gross stake for ACCEPT, the moved amount for deposits, withdrawals and Core exits; null for kinds without a known amount.

status.description: Execution status. QUEUED, IN_FLIGHT, RETRYABLE and UNKNOWN are nonterminal; COMMITTED (on chain), REVERTED and EXPIRED_UNEXECUTED are terminal.

transaction_hash.description: HyperEVM hash of the transaction carrying the operation; null before it is broadcast.

reason.description: Why the operation ended EXPIRED_UNEXECUTED (OperationFailureReason). Absent on any other status, including REVERTED, and on an operation that expired before reasons were recorded.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC time the operation was admitted.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC time the operation last changed.

OperationFailureReason.description: Why an operation ended EXPIRED_UNEXECUTED; nothing it would have done happened. INSUFFICIENT_CASH: an ACCEPT whose taker's money (free vault Cash, or the wallet USDC its approval draws) did not cover the stake when it was to execute; one drawing the wallet waits at least six seconds after the accept arrived for a HyperCore transfer to land; the RFQ fails with the same `reason`. DEADLINE_BEFORE_CLAIM: the venue reached it too late, with too little of its signed deadline left to sign and send it. AUTHORIZATION_TOO_CLOSE: when the venue took it, the chain's clock left too little of its signed deadline to send it. SIGNER_QUOTE_LIFE: its signed deadline could not cover the wait for its place in the sender's queue. SIMULATION_REVERTED: simulated before sending, the vault would have rejected it, for a reason other than INSUFFICIENT_CASH. QUARANTINE_EXPIRED: it was held for review after the signer refused it or its retries ran out, and its signed deadline passed meanwhile. ATTESTATION_EXPIRED: a maker's self-funded attestation expired before its signed transaction arrived. For an ACCEPT every reason but INSUFFICIENT_CASH fails the RFQ as EXPIRED_UNEXECUTED.

operations.description: Operations newest first by creation time.

next_cursor.description: Send as cursor to fetch the next page; null when has_more is false.

has_more.description: True when older operations follow; fetch them with next_cursor.

checkpoint.description: Chain projection the listed states reflect.
Chain projection the operation state reflects.

native.description: The outcome as Hyperliquid listed it, for a client that names markets itself.

pictures.description: Finished pictures for each place the outcome is drawn.

OutcomeNative.description: The outcome exactly as Hyperliquid listed it in the last catalog Totalis recorded it in (the current one while it is listed) or, for an outcome no kept catalog copy holds, as Hyperliquid's settlement record names it.

name.description: Native outcome name, for example template:sportsContestWinner or Recurring.

description.description: Native outcome description; a template instance holds its keyword values as key:value pairs separated by a vertical bar.

side_names.description: Native side names, Yes then No, as listed (template:Yes, template:{shortNameA}); null where the copy Totalis kept predates side names.

question.description: The question the outcome belongs to, from the same catalog; null for a standalone outcome.

native_question_id.description: Hyperliquid question ID; null for an outcome known only from a settlement record that names its question without the ID.

name.description: Native question name, for example template:sportsContestResult.

OutcomePictures.description: Finished pictures for each place an outcome is drawn. null: nothing to picture there; a caller that needs a picture draws a coin from the title's initials.

market.description: The market as a whole, for a card or a header: its question's subject, or the TOTAL glyph for an over/under line.

pick.description: Holding or buying Yes, then No: the side's own subject when it has an image, else the question's subject when it has one, else whichever of them is known (drawn as its coin). A draw carries the DRAW glyph, an over/under line the TOTAL glyph.

pick_no_side.description: Holding or buying the outcome before a side is chosen, by the same rule as `pick` with the option's own subject only: a winner's or spread's sides are its teams, so with no side it shows the question's subject.

own.description: Yes's and No's own subject with no fallback: the team a side of a winner or spread backs, or the option's own subject (a team, a candidate); null where the side has none. Never a glyph.

row.description: The outcome as one option in its question's list: its own subject when it has an image, the DRAW glyph, or, for an option with no subject of its own (Other), the question's subject when it has an image and another option of the question has an image of its own; else null. Decided from the whole question, so a row reads the same alone as in its list. Its subject always has an image; show a list's picture column only while some row has a subject.

teams.description: Participant A's and B's subjects in the outcome's sport when its keywords name both (a game's winner, spread or total, or an option of a contest between them); null otherwise.

contract_version.description: Account-read contract version; always "1" for this response shape.

chain_id.description: EVM chain ID of the deployment the credential is bound to, as a decimal string (999 on HyperEVM Mainnet).

vault.description: Lowercase address of the vault contract of the credential's deployment.

generated_at.description: RFC3339 UTC time the server built this response.

status.description: NOT_CREATED: the account's wallet controls no maker; WALLET_REQUIRED: the account has no single qualifying linked wallet; OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT: several candidate wallets, or the maker's current controller no longer matches; READY: the maker is admitted and current; PENDING: the maker profile awaits admission; RESTRICTED: the maker profile is restricted or closed; SETUP_REQUIRED: a maker controlled by the wallet exists on-chain but has no admitted profile yet.

controller.description: Linked wallet that controls (owns) the maker; absent when the account has no single qualifying linked wallet.

maker.description: The admitted maker and the caller's controller access to it; null unless status is READY, PENDING or RESTRICTED.

ownership.description: Maker ownership status of the caller's account, derived from its linked wallet and indexed on-chain controller evidence.

OwnerProof.description: The account owner's personal_sign or ERC-1271 signature over the exact challenge message. For a maker the owner is its controller; for a personal account, its account wallet.

challenge_id.description: The `challenge_id` of the challenge that was signed.

signature.description: The owner's signature over the challenge's `message`, exactly as returned.

PageCursor.description: Opaque list cursor. Send a previous response's next_cursor back unchanged; never build or parse one.

PageLimit.description: Maximum items in one page. A page may hold fewer, even none, while has_more is true.

content.description: Rendered title and rules of the parent question.

PartnerBalance.description: All time, on every vault Totalis has run in this environment. Each fee is priced at the terms in force on its UTC day.

share_bps.description: Your current share of total fees in basis points, or null before your first terms.

fees.description: Every fee charged on your positions.

unpriced_fees.description: The part of fees charged before your first terms, which earns nothing.

accrued.description: What you have earned: each terms period's fees times its share, rounded down.

paid.description: What counts as paid: what landed, or a payout's whole amount while it is open or a transfer is pending.

owed.description: accrued minus paid; negative after an overpayment. Totalis decides when to pay.

day.description: The UTC day, by block time.

share_bps.description: The terms in force that day, or null before your first terms.

taker_fees.description: Fees charged on opening them, atomic USDC.

winnings_fees.description: Fees charged on their claimed winnings, atomic USDC.

buyback_fees.description: Fees charged on their cash-outs, atomic USDC.

total_fees.description: All three together, atomic USDC: what your share is of.

cashouts.description: Times the account that opened one of these positions cashed it out, whether the vault bought it back or a maker bought it.

cashout_volume.description: What those cash-outs paid, atomic USDC.

active_traders.description: Accounts that opened a position through your codes. In totals, each account counts once over the range.

PartnerFill.description: One fee event on a position opened through your builder codes. Amounts are atomic USDC (6 decimals) decimal strings.

kind.description: ACCEPT: the position opened, and amount is its stake with the taker fee. CLAIM: a claim paid amount, before the profit fee. CASH_OUT: the vault bought the position back for amount.

wallet.description: The wallet that acted: the one that opened or claimed, or the seller.

position_id.description: The position, as GET /v1/me/positions names it.

legs.description: The position's legs: one for a single, more for a Combo.

amount.description: What the event moved, as kind says.

fee.description: The fee the vault took: the taker fee on ACCEPT, the profit fee on CLAIM and CASH_OUT. Zero when none was due.

stake.description: The position's stake after the taker fee, as it opened.

payout.description: What the position pays if every leg wins; stake over payout is the price it opened at.

share_bps.description: Your share of fees, in basis points, under the terms in force on the fill's UTC day; null before your first terms. Each terms period's share is rounded down once, so per-fill shares do not add up exactly to what you are owed.

log_index.description: The event's log index in its block; with block_number it identifies the fill.

next_cursor.description: Send it as cursor for the fills after this page. It follows the last fill even when has_more is false, so keep it and read again later, with the same from and a later to, for new fills. Null only when no fill has been returned yet.

has_more.description: Whether more fills follow in the range.

period_start.description: First day the payout is for.

period_end.description: Last day the payout is for, inclusive.

payout_address.description: Where it is sent: your payout address when it was queued.

counted.description: What it counts as paid: the whole amount while open or pending, then what landed.

status.description: OPEN until its transfer is checked on-chain; SETTLED once it is; CANCELLED if dropped before anything moved.

closed_at.description: When it settled or was cancelled.

transfers.description: The USDC transactions sent for it on HyperEVM, oldest first.

PartnerReport.description: A partner's own report: the figures Totalis pays from. Amounts are atomic USDC (6 decimals) decimal strings.

balance.description: What you have earned, been paid and are owed, all time.

users.description: Your users, all time. Active traders and new accounts in the range are in totals and days.

open_positions.description: Positions opened through your codes that are open now and still held by the account that opened them.

stake.description: Their stake after the taker fee, atomic USDC.

terms.description: Your terms, oldest first; each holds from its day until the next.

from.description: First UTC day of the range.

totals.description: The range's days added up, except active_traders, which counts each account once.

days.description: Each UTC day in the range with fees, cash-outs, traders or new accounts, oldest first; other days are absent.

payouts.description: Every payout to you, newest first.

effective_from.description: First UTC day these terms price.

share_bps.description: Your share of total fees, in basis points.

transaction_hash.description: The HyperEVM transaction that sent it.

outcome.description: PENDING until checked; LANDED once its block is final; DEAD if it never landed.

moved.description: What it paid you once landed.

resolved_at.description: When it was found landed or dead, or null while pending.

id.description: The event's id, as the webhook-id header carried it; dedupe on it.

kind.description: The event kind, such as position.opened or balance.updated.

event.description: The event body exactly as Totalis posts it to the webhook.

status.description: PENDING while Totalis still sends it, DELIVERED once the webhook answered 2xx, FAILED after the last attempt failed.

attempts.description: How many times Totalis has sent it.

delivered_at.description: When the webhook accepted it, or null.

events.description: Events in the order Totalis queued them, oldest first.

next_cursor.description: Send it as cursor for the events after this page. It follows the last event even when has_more is false, so keep it and read again later for new events. Null only when no event has been returned yet.

context.description: Freshness of this read: the oldest source observation and one freshness for every amount in the response.

from.description: Inclusive RFC3339 start of the requested period, echoed from the query.

through.description: Exclusive RFC3339 end of the requested period, echoed from the query.

recognition.description: P&L recognition rule: realized at economic close (settlement or sell-back), version 1. Claims do not recognize P&L again.

history_from.description: Earliest from this maker's periods can start at and still be complete: the later of where retained vault history and venue workflows begin, or the maker's opening block if later still. Request from=history_from for an all-time period. Null while vault history is unavailable.

closed_position_count.description: Positions economically closed in the period, as a decimal string; null when settled_net_stake is null.

won_position_count.description: Closes in the period the maker won (positive maker P&L), as a decimal string; null exactly when closed_position_count is null.

lost_position_count.description: Closes in the period the maker lost (negative maker P&L), as a decimal string; null exactly when closed_position_count is null.

even_position_count.description: Closes in the period with zero maker P&L, as a decimal string; null exactly when closed_position_count is null. Won, lost and even add up to closed_position_count.

settled_net_stake.description: Net stake released by economic closes in the period.

gross_trading_pnl.description: Signed maker trading P&L from closes in the period (net stake minus effective payout).

gross_winning_pnl.description: Sum of the maker P&L of the period's closes the maker won (each positive), so never negative. gross_winning_pnl + gross_losing_pnl = gross_trading_pnl; profit factor is gross_winning_pnl / -gross_losing_pnl.

gross_losing_pnl.description: Sum of the maker P&L of the period's closes the maker lost (each negative), so never positive.

attributed_fees.description: Fees the maker paid in the period. Taker fees are not maker expenses.

external_inflows.description: Deposits into the maker vault in the period; never P&L.

external_outflows.description: Executed maker withdrawals in the period; never P&L.

series.description: Cumulative net realized P&L at UTC day boundaries within the requested interval, from the same revision as totals, in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC): the opening zero point at from, one point per UTC day with closes or maker-paid fees, then through if no day ends there. Each point carries the closes since the previous one, so a day with closes is told apart from the synthetic endpoints. Empty when net_trading_pnl is null.

at.description: Point time: from for the opening zero point, then the end of each UTC day with closes (capped at through), then through.

net_trading_pnl.description: Cumulative signed net trading P&L from from up to at, in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC).

closed_position_count.description: Closes since the previous point, as a decimal string: the day's closes for a day point ("0" only on a day whose maker-paid fees moved P&L); "0" for the opening point and for a through point added after the last such day.

net_trading_pnl_change.description: Net trading P&L of those closes: net_trading_pnl minus the previous point's. A day point with closes is a real close day even when this is "0".

Performance.description: Maker realized performance for a period. Every period aggregate is null unless the whole period is covered by reconciled history.

items.description: Keys of the account, oldest first.

kind.description: The account kind: `PARTICIPANT` for a personal account.

account.description: The account the key acts for.

kind.description: GLYPH: a mark of the client's own, never artwork.

glyph.description: DRAW: a contest's draw outcome. TOTAL: an over/under line, drawn as Over for Yes and Under for No where the side is known.

kind.description: SUBJECT: a subject described once in the answer's `subjects`.

PnL.description: Cumulative trading P&L of the account Portfolio shows, computed on read: Core trading plus Combos closed in the deployment's vault. Points are cumulative since tracked_since, not rebased: a window's change is its last point minus its first. Deposits, withdrawals and moves between Core and the vault never move it.

tracked_since.description: Where P&L starts: the later of the start of the account's recorded Core history and 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, the first whole day of stored values; P&L is cumulative from here. It does not prove that history is complete: a fill gap, an unbridged cash gap or holdings the history cannot reproduce make the read UNAVAILABLE with tracked_since still set. Null while the wallet is not yet observed, with no points and a STALE context.

points.description: Ascending instants: the window start (never before tracked_since), every round UTC step boundary inside it (1D every 15 minutes, 1W every hour, 1M every 6 hours, ALL an adaptive step of at most 200 points), then the read time valued at live marks.

pnl.description: Cumulative P&L from tracked_since up to at, in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC), rounded once, half away from zero. Null when a share held at at has no known value, when at precedes the first known value of shares held at tracked_since (every earlier point is null), or when the read is UNAVAILABLE; null is never zero.

context.description: Freshness of this read. as_of is the valuation instant, the last point's at: it values the history at that instant's marks, and STALE says a source lags. UNAVAILABLE nulls every point.

Position.description: A position as an account reads it: GET /v1/me/positions and GET /v1/me/positions/{position_id}, a maker key's included.

context.description: Freshness of this read: the oldest source observation and one freshness for every amount in the response.

PositionFields.description: What every read of a position carries: Position on an account's reads, and MakerPosition, which adds the maker's view, on the maker's.

position_id.description: Position ID: the contract's ticketId (bytes32 hex), which is the `quote_id` of the quote accepted to open it: the EIP-712 digest of that quote under its vault's domain, so it names one position across every vault.

vault_address.description: Lowercase vault contract address the position is on. An account's positions span every vault the deployment has served: the active one, one running off and closed ones.

cashout_available.description: Whether this position takes a cash-out. It is false on a vault running off, which refuses one (`STATE_CONFLICT`) and pays out automatically when the position settles, and on a free Combo (`golden`), which is never cashed out (`GOLDEN_CASHOUT_REFUSED`). Whether this position can be cashed out now also depends on its status.

golden.description: Whether this position is a free Combo: a promotion paid its stake and gave it away, and it stays one whoever holds it now. Its `net_stake` is what the promotion paid, never its holder's money; what it pays at settlement is the holder's. It is never cashed out.

maker_id.description: Maker that wrote the position, as a decimal string.

status.description: OPEN: not yet known eligible for settlement; AWAITING_SETTLEMENT: every leg resolved, or the payout with every unresolved leg counted as a win already rounds down to zero, but no settlement observed; SETTLED_UNCLAIMED: settled with profit still unclaimed; CLOSED: closed by zero-profit settlement, final claim or sell-back.

fee_bps.description: Profit fee in basis points, fixed when the position opened. The holder claims unclaimed_profit minus unclaimed_profit * fee_bps / 10000.

reason.description: How a CLOSED position closed: CLAIM (final claim of winnings) or SELL_BACK (bought back by the maker). Null otherwise, including direct zero-profit settlement closes and closes without retained evidence.

net_stake.description: Stake after the taker entry fee.

acquisition_cost.description: What the current owner paid for the whole position: the price of the latest transfer to them, or the gross stake with the entry fee if they have held it since opening. Settlement, claims and sell-back don't change it. Null when retained chain history has a gap that could hide a transfer. P&L compares it with what the owner gets back, settlement_payout or cashout_price, less the profit fee of fee_bps on the amount above net_stake, whatever the owner paid.

payout.description: Payout if every leg wins, as the maker signed it in the quote; the maker's initial exposure is payout minus net_stake.

settlement_payout.description: Settlement payout observed on-chain; null before settlement and for sold-back positions.

unclaimed_profit.description: Gross profit still claimable; "0" unless SETTLED_UNCLAIMED. The holder receives unclaimed_profit minus unclaimed_profit * fee_bps / 10000.

cashout_price.description: Cash-out price paid when the position was sold back; null unless reason is SELL_BACK.

legs.description: Position legs in ascending outcome_id order, with each leg's resolution.

created_at.description: RFC3339 time of the position's opening event; lists order by it, newest first.

updated_at.description: RFC3339 time of the position's latest lifecycle event.

settlement_kind.description: Settlement result: LOSS (zero payout), PARTIAL (payout below net stake), WIN (payout at or above net stake) or EARLY_LOST (lost before every leg resolved). Null before settlement, for sell-backs, or when historical evidence is missing.

protocol_fees.description: Fees the vault took on this position so far, all paid by its owners and none by the maker: the taker entry fee at opening plus the profit fee withheld from each claim and from a sell-back. Null when retained history has a gap that could hide one.

unclaimed_profit.description: An available unclaimed_profit is "0" for OPEN, AWAITING_SETTLEMENT and CLOSED positions.
An available unclaimed_profit is positive for SETTLED_UNCLAIMED positions.

context.description: Freshness of this read: the oldest source observation and one freshness for every amount in the response.

items.description: Positions on this page, newest created_at first, then position_id descending.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, bound to this response's snapshot; null on the last page. Send it back unchanged as cursor.

has_more.description: True when another page exists; true exactly when next_cursor is non-null.

total_count.description: Exact number of positions in the whole filtered snapshot (not just this page), as a decimal string.

PositiveInt64.description: Positive generation or version bounded by signed int64 storage.

content.description: Rendered title and rules of the market itself.

parent.description: Parent question details for a NAMED or FALLBACK market; null for a standalone market.

sides.description: Display labels of the YES and NO sides, in that order.

ProfilePictureUrl.description: A profile picture: an X picture (XPictureUrl), or one the account uploaded, served by this API at /v1/pictures/{sha256}.jpg as a 400x400 JPEG named by the SHA-256 of its bytes. Clients may cache it for 5 minutes, so a removed picture disappears within 5 minutes.

catalog_generation.description: Catalog generation the question and its markets were read from.

title.description: Display title derived from the question definition.

outcome_ids.description: Outcome IDs of the question's markets in the current catalog.

status.description: ACTIVE when any market is active, CLOSED when none is active and at least one is closed, UNSUPPORTED otherwise.

category.description: Display category, or null when the question is not mapped to one.

subcategory.description: Display subcategory slug within the category; null when unmapped or not subdivided.

markets.description: The question's markets in the current catalog. In a market detail, the requested market is given once as market and is not repeated here.

relationships.description: Relationships between the question's markets; empty when it has none in the catalog.

estimated_live_until.description: End of the question's in-play window when it is a scheduled single contest, as its browse card shows it: its markets' shared scheduled start (dates.scheduled_event_at) plus its league's reviewed usual game length, unless the live game feed shows the game in play (then at least 15 minutes past the read, extended until it ends) or over (then the moment it was first seen over, or the start if that was earlier). Never a trading cutoff, closure or settlement. Present before the contest starts. Null for anything else: tournaments, leagues without a reviewed length, markets that are not contests or lines, or markets that disagree on the start.

scoreboard.description: The question's game as the live game feed last read it, for display only. Null when it has no estimated_live_until, the feed does not cover or could not match the game, or its last reading of an unfinished game is stale.

kind.description: How the listed markets relate. SAME_QUESTION means they are all outcomes of this native question; the other kinds are reserved.

outcome_ids.description: Outcome IDs covered by the relationship.

Quote.description: One live, unsigned quote on an RFQ, told apart by `kind`. List quotes, the account snapshot's quotes and `QUOTE_CREATED` carry the same item.

status.description: The quote's status after the call. `CANCELLED`: off the RFQ, now or earlier (you cancelled or declined it, its acceptance timed out, or you missed a confirm). `REPLACED`: a newer quote of yours replaced it. `ACCEPTED`: you already confirmed it, so it cannot be cancelled; returned with `409`.

quote_id.description: ID of the created quote: the digest of its terms. The quote gets a new ID each time the venue renews it; any of them cancels the quote.

QuoteCreated.description: The created quote's ID. The venue keeps it live and renews it until you cancel it or the RFQ ends.

submitted_count.description: Quotes the maker published in the period (of the requested kind), every replacement counted, whatever their status.

filled_count.description: Of those, quotes whose trade committed on chain (status FILLED).

fill_rate_bps.description: floor(filled_count * 10000 / submitted_count) in basis points; null when submitted_count is 0.

QuoteFillRate.description: Fill rate of the period's quotes; status filters do not apply to it.

context.description: Freshness of this read. Quotes are venue rows read now; FILLED and FAILED follow the vault projection, so as_of is its checkpoint and freshness is STALE while it lags.

from.description: Inclusive RFC3339 start of the period on submitted_at, echoed from the query.

through.description: Exclusive RFC3339 end of the period, echoed from the query.

fill_rate.description: The period's fill rate, on a list's first page (no cursor); null on later pages.

items.description: Quotes on this page, newest submitted_at first. Each status is read when the page is.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; null on the last page. Send it back unchanged as cursor with the same filters.

has_more.description: True exactly when next_cursor is non-null. A status-filtered page reads at most 1,000 quotes, so it may hold fewer items than limit, even none, while has_more is true.

QuoteHistory.description: Every quote the maker published in a period, not only live ones, with the period's fill rate.

quote_id.description: Quote ID: the digest the maker signs on confirmation (bytes32 hex).

kind.description: ENTRY opens a position; CASHOUT buys one back (SELL_BACK).

cashout_kind.description: For a CASHOUT quote, SELL_BACK: the position's own maker buys it back. null for ENTRY.

status.description: Where the quote stands now. OPEN, AWAITING_CONFIRMATION and ACCEPTED can still change; every other status is final. FILLED is the only status in which the quote traded.

submitted_at.description: When the venue admitted the quote; lists order by it, newest first.

accepted_at.description: When the taker accepted the quote; null if no taker did.

resolved_at.description: When the quote reached its status: the trade's chain receipt for FILLED and FAILED, the confirmation deadline for TIMED_OUT, the winning selection for NOT_SELECTED, the earlier of the quote's and the RFQ's expiry for EXPIRED. Null while OPEN, AWAITING_CONFIRMATION or ACCEPTED, and for DECLINED, CANCELLED, REPLACED and RFQ_CANCELLED, whose time the venue does not record.

operation_id.description: The trade's operation once the maker confirmed; null otherwise.

position_id.description: For ENTRY, the position the quote opened once FILLED (its quote_id); for CASHOUT, the position being cashed out; null otherwise.

outcome_id.description: HIP-4 outcome ID of the leg.

legs.description: An ENTRY quote's legs in the RFQ's order; null for CASHOUT.

stake.description: ENTRY: the taker's gross stake, before the entry fee. Null for CASHOUT. The quoted odds are payout / stake.

net_stake.description: ENTRY: stake less the taker entry fee floor(stake * taker_fee_bps / 10000), what the vault escrows. Null for CASHOUT, or when the quote's fee was never admitted.

payout.description: ENTRY: what the taker receives if every leg wins. Null for CASHOUT.

maker_risk.description: ENTRY: what the maker stands to pay, payout minus net_stake. Null when net_stake is.

price.description: CASHOUT: the price offered for the whole position. Null for ENTRY.

QuoteHistoryItem.description: One quote the maker published, display fields only; never a signature. A decline carries no reason: the maker's answer records none.

QuoteHistoryStatus.description: Where the quote stands now. OPEN: live and acceptable. AWAITING_CONFIRMATION: the taker accepted it and the maker has not answered within its two-second deadline yet. ACCEPTED: the maker confirmed and the trade is queued or on its way to chain. FILLED: the trade committed on chain. FAILED: the trade reverted or expired unexecuted. DECLINED: the maker declined the acceptance. TIMED_OUT: the maker did not answer the acceptance in time. CANCELLED: the maker withdrew the quote. REPLACED: the maker's newer quote on the same RFQ replaced it. EXPIRED: it or its RFQ lapsed unaccepted. NOT_SELECTED: the RFQ's taker accepted another quote first. RFQ_CANCELLED: the taker cancelled or replaced the RFQ.

quotes.description: Live quotes on this RFQ in creation order, at most 100. Rank them yourself. Every listed quote can be accepted. Left out: entry quotes about to lapse (the venue renews them first), cash-out quotes within 22 seconds of expiry, a quote whose acceptance timed out, and every quote on a cash-out RFQ that already has an accepted one.

maker_id.description: On-chain maker ID of the quoting maker.

legs.description: Legs the quote covers; must equal the RFQ legs in order. The signed Leg encodes outcome_id as uint32 and side as uint8, 0 for YES and 1 for NO.

stake.description: Taker stake in atomic USDC (6 decimals), before taker fees.

payout.description: Gross amount the position pays if every leg wins, in atomic USDC (6 decimals), before the profit fee.

fee_bps.description: Profit fee in basis points, charged at claim on the winning profit (payout minus net stake).

taker_fee_bps.description: Entry fee in basis points taken from the stake at accept: net stake is stake minus floor(stake * taker_fee_bps / 10000).

taker.description: Wallet that must sign the accept and will own the position.

expiry.description: Unix seconds after which the quote can no longer be accepted.

salt.description: Random uint256, as a decimal string, that makes each signed quote unique.

QuoteTerms.description: Entry terms a maker quotes; they mirror the signed Quote and TakerAccept structs field for field.

as_of.description: RFC3339 observation time of the oldest source this read used.

freshness.description: Freshness of the whole read. CURRENT: every source is fresh and reconciled. STALE: a source lags or has not reconciled, such as a catching-up projection, a pending reorg rescan or a period not fully covered; amounts may be displayed with their age but never authorize an action. UNAVAILABLE: a required source could not be read, so the amounts it backs are null.

ReadContext.description: Freshness of the read. Pages of one list share the snapshot bound into their cursor.

RealQuestionId.description: A real native question identifier; the standalone NO_QUESTION sentinel is excluded.

RecurringPrice.description: Exact deployer price text; never reformatted or rounded.

expiry.description: Exact deployer settlement instant in Unix seconds; no safety buffer is applied.

target_price.description: A native PRICE_BINARY round settles YES when the interpolated mark price is at or above this value. A template stream round carries the template's threshold and settles YES only when the settlement price is strictly above it.

price_thresholds.description: Ascending PRICE_BUCKET boundaries; the three buckets cover `< P1`, `[P1, P2)` and `>= P2`.

native_question_id.description: Parent question of a bucket round; null for a standalone binary round.

markets.description: Markets of the round: one STANDALONE market for a binary round, or three NAMED buckets and one FALLBACK for a bucket round.

catalog_state.description: NOT_LISTED means the round is durably recorded but absent from the current catalog generation, so its market and question routes return 404.

series.description: Recurring series the round belongs to.

current.description: The round that contains the requested market or question.

previous.description: Nearest earlier recorded round of the same series, for a stream the nearest earlier round with the same period; null unless previous_state is AVAILABLE.

previous_state.description: BEFORE_RECORDED_HISTORY means Totalis never observed an earlier round; it never claims that none existed. CONFLICTED means the nearest earlier round was observed but its recorded definition is withheld.

next.description: Nearest later recorded round of the same series, for a stream the nearest later round with the same period; null unless next_state is AVAILABLE.

next_state.description: NONE_RECORDED means Totalis has not observed a later round; it never claims none was published. CONFLICTED means the nearest later round was observed but its recorded definition is withheld.

outcome_id.description: Hyperliquid outcome ID of the round's market.

role.description: STANDALONE for the single market of a binary round, NAMED for a price bucket of a bucket round, FALLBACK for the bucket question's fallback outcome.

index.description: Bucket position the child market states for itself; null unless the role is NAMED.

network.description: Hyperliquid network the series runs on.

kind.description: PRICE_BINARY for a single above-or-below round, PRICE_BUCKET for a three-bucket price range question. A template stream is always PRICE_BINARY.

underlying.description: Deployer instrument name, optionally prefixed with a provider namespace; the template's perp for a stream.

period.description: Round length as a number followed by m (minutes), h (hours) or d (days), for example 1d. A stream's period is 5m, 15m or 1h.

stream.description: The deployer template stream whose recorded cadence makes these rounds recurring; null for a native Hyperliquid recurring series.

RecurringSeries.description: Hyperliquid guarantees at most one native recurring series per network, kind, underlying and period. A template stream is identified by its stream, so several can share an underlying and period.

stream_id.description: Stable key of the stream: its network, venue, quote asset, template and every template field except the round's threshold and time.

venue.description: Deployer venue that lists the stream; null for a native deployer.

template.description: Deployer template every round of the stream uses.

price_description.description: Price the template settles on, exactly as the deployer wrote it; null when the network's template has no such field.

seconds.description: Length in seconds of the settlement TWAP ending at the round's expiry; null when the network's template has no such field.

RecurringStream.description: A repeating standalone deployer template market. A round joins the recurring series only when it and the stream's two previous recorded expiries each hold exactly one market, are evenly spaced by 5, 15 or 60 minutes, and Totalis first saw the round at most two periods before its expiry. It loses that period once later records break any of these, such as a second market at its expiry or at one of the two before it, or an earlier first sighting. Rounds listed with several thresholds at one expiry never qualify.

availability.description: AVAILABLE: a qualified reference price has been observed for this side.

quality.description: How the reference price was derived: BOOK_MID from the order book or best bid and offer (the midpoint, or the mark when best_bid or best_ask is null), MARK_PRICE from the mark price, ALL_MIDS_FALLBACK from the all-mids fallback, TRADE from executed trades.

value.description: Reference price of this side as an integer: the book midpoint, or mark when the book is one-sided or empty, which is published only while mark is known. Divide by scale for the probability price between 0 and 1.

best_bid.description: Best bid at scale when the book has bids, otherwise null.

best_ask.description: Best ask at scale when the book has asks, otherwise null.

last_trade.description: Price of the latest book execution on this side at scale, kept across restarts; a fill prints on both sides at prices summing to scale. Null when no trade is known.

last_trade_at.description: Hyperliquid time of last_trade, RFC 3339 UTC; null exactly when last_trade is null.

chance.description: Crowd probability at scale: the newest evidence (an execution, or the book midpoint while best_ask - best_bid is at most 10% of scale) kept within [best_bid, best_ask]. On a book wider than 50% of scale, one-sided or empty, it is null once that evidence is more than 20 minutes old. Null before any evidence. The midpoint rounds half to even, so YES and NO chances sum to scale. chance_basis says which applied.

chance_basis.description: Where chance comes from: MID, the current book midpoint; LAST_TRADE, last_trade inside the current book; HELD, earlier evidence kept within the current book (a midpoint the book no longer supports, or evidence clamped to best_bid or best_ask). Null exactly when chance is null.

mark.description: Value of one held share at scale: chance when known, else best_bid, else 0 when only asks exist; null when no book is known. Not a price a trade receives.

scale.description: Divisor for value, best_bid, best_ask, last_trade, chance and mark; currently 1000000000000000000 (18 decimals).

freshness.description: FRESH when received within the last 15 seconds, otherwise STALE.

received_at.description: When Totalis received the observation, RFC 3339 UTC.

availability.description: UNAVAILABLE: no qualified reference price exists for this side; reason says why.

reason.description: NOT_OBSERVED: no price seen yet; AMBIGUOUS_SOURCE: the source gave conflicting values; STALE_GENERATION: the last price belongs to an older feed generation; UNSUPPORTED_MARKET: the market is not supported; SOURCE_UNQUALIFIED: the copy carries no live price, as in cached catalog pages and finished markets that left the catalog.

freshness.description: Always UNKNOWN while no price is available.

received_at.description: Last update time of the market record this state was derived from, RFC 3339 UTC; 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z in cached catalog copies.

amount.description: Reserved amount in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC).

status.description: ACTIVE: held and not yet reflected on-chain; UNKNOWN: outcome unknown, still counted as held.

Reservation.description: A venue admission reservation on the maker vault.

availability.description: AVAILABLE: the native result was read successfully.

result_state.description: RECOGNIZED_NONNUMERIC_OBSERVED: the native market recorded a recognized result that carries no numeric payout factor.

recorded_at_block.description: HyperEVM block number of the native read that observed this result.

evidence_digest.description: SHA-256 over the chain, contracts, block number and hash, outcome and result of the native read that observed this result.

availability.description: AVAILABLE: the native result was read successfully.

result_state.description: NUMERIC_RECORDED: the native market recorded a numeric payout for the YES side.

yes_factor_numerator.description: YES payout as a fraction of factor_scale; 100000000 pays YES in full, 0 pays NO in full.

recorded_at_block.description: HyperEVM block number of the native read that observed this result.

evidence_digest.description: SHA-256 over the chain, contracts, block number and hash, outcome and result of the native read that observed this result.

availability.description: UNAVAILABLE: the native result could not be read; reason says why.

reason.description: NOT_QUERIED: not read yet; NATIVE_READ_FAILED: the on-chain read failed; RPC_UNAVAILABLE: no RPC provider answered; MALFORMED_RETURN: the contract returned an unexpected shape; PROVIDER_DISAGREEMENT: providers returned different results; UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION: the outcome uses an unsupported protocol version.

availability.description: AVAILABLE: the native result was read successfully.

result_state.description: UNRESOLVED: the native market has not recorded a result.

Retry.description: NEVER: stop. BACKOFF: resend the same request with the same Idempotency-Key after Retry-After. REFRESH: re-read state, then send a new request with a new Idempotency-Key.

rfqs.description: Open RFQs on this page, in listing order.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null when has_more is false.

has_more.description: True when another page follows; send next_cursor to read it.

overlap_seconds.description: How long the old key keeps working after the rotation, 0 to 86400 seconds; 3600 when omitted.

expires_in_days.description: The replacement's lifetime in days, 1 to 90, or 0 for no expiry; 30 when omitted.

proof.description: The account owner's signature over the challenge for exactly this request without `proof`.

RotateKeyRequest.description: Every rotation needs a fresh owner proof over exactly this request without proof. The replacement inherits the predecessor's account, label and scopes.

rotated_from.description: The rotated key, the `key_id` in the path.

vault_address.description: The vault running off, lowercase; the Exit's EIP-712 verifying contract (domain TotalisParlay, version 1, chain ID of the deployment).

vault_free.description: Free cash in that vault in atomic USDC (6 decimals): at most what one Exit may move.

pending_core_exits.description: Exits from that vault leaving or awaiting their HyperCore credit, in atomic USDC.

freshness.description: CURRENT when that vault's projection is current; STALE when it lags, so the amounts may be behind and never authorize a claim.

claim.description: The account's claim from that vault still in flight, to resume after a reload; follow it with Get operation. Null when none is.

vault_address.description: The vault running off the cash leaves.

operation.description: The claim's WITHDRAW_USER operation; follow it with Get operation.

RunOffClaimCommand.description: The account wallet's signed EIP-712 Exit of the account's cash in a vault running off, to the account's own wallet; Totalis relays it and pays the gas. The credential names the account: the Exit's account and to are both the credential's account wallet, so the body carries only the vault and the signed terms.

vault_address.description: The vault running off, from run_off in Get balances: the Exit's EIP-712 verifying contract. Any other address is INVALID_REQUEST.

amount.description: Atomic USDC (6 decimals) to move; at most vault_free. An account whose wallet is not a Totalis embedded wallet moves at least 1 USDC (1000000).

expiry.description: Exit expiry in Unix seconds; at least 5 seconds ahead and at most 3600 seconds ahead, less a 5-second clock-skew margin.

salt.description: Caller-chosen uint256 as a decimal string that makes the signed Exit unique.

signature.description: Signature by the account wallet over the EIP-712 Exit(account,to,amount,expiry,salt) digest for that vault's domain, with account and to both the credential's account wallet; ECDSA or ERC-1271 contract signature bytes.

Scale.description: Positive base-10 scale for an integer value.

Scope.description: One permission a key can hold. Each operation lists the scopes it requires, and a key holds only scopes that apply to its account, as the capabilities routes list. `operations:read` is reserved and never issued; `maker:access:read` is no longer issued and has no effect on a key that still carries it.

ScopeList.description: Replay needs a feed the key can read: account:stream or rfq:read for a personal account, vault:read, quote:read or rfq:read for a maker.

Scoreboard.description: A matchup's game as the live game feed last read it, for display only: never a result, settlement or trading input. A reading of an unfinished game is served only while under 75 seconds old; a FINAL, POSTPONED or CANCELLED one stays. A field the feed lacks is null, never a guess.

status.description: The game's phase. BREAK is a pause in play: half time, between periods or innings.

period.description: Display label of the period in play, or just ended during a BREAK: Q1-Q4, OT, 2OT (basketball, American football); P1-P3, OT, SO (hockey); Top 7th, Bottom 7th, Mid 7th, End 7th (baseball); HT at half time; ET or PEN in soccer extra time or penalties. On a FINAL only how it went beyond regulation (OT, 2OT, SO, AET, PEN, an extra inning such as 10th), else null.

clock.description: Game clock while LIVE: remaining time such as 4:58, or soccer minutes such as 67' and 90+6'. Null otherwise and in baseball.

outs.description: Outs in the current half-inning while a baseball game is LIVE, when the feed has them.

competitors.description: Both sides in the order the matchup names them: a game's participants, else a question's or market's 'A v B' title order. Never the feed's home and away order.

last_play.description: The feed's text of the latest play while the game is in play, in English, cut to 200 characters ending in an ellipsis when longer.

stream.description: The game's official live broadcast while it is unfinished: an organizer's channel that the backend saw on air showing this game, within the last 2 minutes. Absent when no channel is known to show it, and once the game is FINAL, POSTPONED or CANCELLED.

refreshed_at.description: When the backend last read this from the feed.

name.description: The participant's name as our catalog spells it, cut to 96 characters ending in an ellipsis when longer.

score.description: Current score; null before the game starts and when the feed has none.

shootout_score.description: Soccer penalty shootout goals, separate from score; null when there was no shootout.

operation_id.description: Operation the transaction was attached to.

status.description: Operation status after the transaction was attached.

transaction_hash.description: Hash of the attached signed transaction.

signed_transaction.description: Raw signed EIP-1559 (type 2) transaction as lowercase hex. It must target the vault on the environment chain with zero value and the operation's exact calldata. The contract call is permissionless: the signature inside the transaction is what authorizes it.

kind.description: Always `SELL_BACK`: your vault buys the position back.

deadline.description: Confirm before this instant, an RFC3339 UTC timestamp. A later answer cannot reopen the acceptance.

sell_back.description: Accepted sell-back terms; sign them as `SellBack`.

SellBackMakerAcceptance.description: An owner's accept of your sell-back quote.
SellBackMakerAcceptance.title: Sell-back acceptance

kind.description: Always `SELL_BACK`: the backing maker buys the position back.

sequence.description: Venue-wide publication sequence number; a higher value was created later.

price.description: What the maker pays to close the position, in atomic USDC (6 decimals).

sell_back.description: The sell-back terms the taker signs as the EIP-712 `SellBack` struct, whose digest is `quote_id`, to accept.

signing.description: What the taker signs to accept. The SDK signs it for you.

SellBackQuote.description: A cash-out offer from the maker that backs the position: its vault buys the position back for `price`.
SellBackQuote.title: Sell-back quote

position_id.description: Position the quote is for; the signed SellBack names it ticketId.

price.description: Buyback price the original maker pays the owner to close the position, in atomic USDC (6 decimals).

owner.description: Current position owner, who sells the position back.

expiry.description: Unix seconds after which the quote can no longer be executed.

salt.description: Random uint256, as a decimal string, that makes each signed quote unique.

leg_state.description: Position leg state, legStateOf(legs, 500000), the quote was priced against.

SellBackTerms.description: Sell-back terms: the underwriting maker buys the position back and it closes. They mirror the signed SellBack struct.

SeriesId.description: Series key: the first 16 lowercase hex characters of the SHA-256 of v1|network|template|subject|expiry, where network is mainnet or testnet; for a price series template is binaryPrice or priceTouch, subject the perp name and expiry its decimal Unix seconds; for an IPO ladder template is companyIpoFirstDayMarketCap, subject the trimmed company and expiry the listing deadline's decimal Unix seconds. Thresholds and membership are not part of the key.

SeriesMarket.description: A series or game member: a standalone market with no Hyperliquid question.

native_question_id.description: Always null: a member has no Hyperliquid question.

side.description: Market side the label belongs to, YES or NO.

label.description: Display label for the side; null when a templated name cannot be rendered from a qualified template.
The subject's name, for alternative text.

monogram.description: The subject's short mark, drawn on a coin when it has no image, while its image loads or when it fails.

image.description: The subject's artwork; null for a known subject without any, drawn as its coin.

fit.description: ICON: a logo inset on a transparent square, drawn whole. PHOTO: a photo that fills its circle.

variants.description: Square WebP renditions at 64, 128 and 256 pixels, in that order. Their URLs never change content.

palette.description: The image's chromatic colors, most used first, for team and chart line colors; absent where imagery recorded none. A line wears its side's `own` subject's palette when that subject has an image, or, when it is a chart's only line and its side's own subject has none, `market`'s; a line whose `pick` is a glyph wears none.

SubjectKey.description: An imagery subject's key: its kind, a colon and its normalized name, such as team:detroit lions.

Subjects.description: Each subject a picture of the answer names, once, by key.

chain_id.description: HyperEVM chain ID for the transaction: 998 testnet or 999 mainnet.

data.description: Canonical ABI-encoded calldata built by the server; lowercase hex.

value.description: Native value in wei; always zero.

label.description: Your name for the key, 1 to 80 characters.

scopes.description: Permissions the key holds; each must apply to the account, as the capabilities route lists. Send `scopes` or `preset`, not both.

preset.description: A documented scope set instead of `scopes`. The owner signs, and the key holds, the scopes it expands to.

expires_in_days.description: Lifetime in days, 1 to 90, or 0 for no expiry; 30 when omitted.

UnsignedCreateKeyRequest.description: The exact key request the account owner signs. Scopes must apply to the account.

UnsignedMetric.description: Non-negative amount in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC); null when it could not be established, never zero in its place.

overlap_seconds.description: How long the old key keeps working after the rotation, 0 to 86400 seconds; 3600 when omitted.

expires_in_days.description: The replacement's lifetime in days, 1 to 90, or 0 for no expiry; 30 when omitted.

UnsignedRotateKeyRequest.description: The exact rotation request the account owner signs; the replacement inherits the old key's account, label and scopes.

Username.description: 3 to 20 lowercase letters, digits or underscores. Unique across accounts.

VaultWithdrawal.description: Owner-signed EIP-712 Exit that moves the withdrawal's shortfall from the vault to the embedded wallet; Totalis relays it and pays gas. The signed Exit's `account` and `to` are both the caller's embedded wallet, which the venue fills in.

amount.description: Shortfall in atomic USDC (6 decimals): the withdrawal amount minus spendable wallet USDC; must be greater than zero.

expiry.description: Exit expiry in Unix seconds; must be at least 5 seconds ahead and at most 3600 seconds ahead, less a 5-second clock-skew margin.

salt.description: Caller-chosen uint256 as a decimal string that makes the signed Exit unique.

signature.description: Signature by the embedded wallet over the EIP-712 `Exit(account,to,amount,expiry,salt)` digest, with `account` and `to` the wallet; ECDSA or ERC-1271 contract signature bytes.

status.description: Account status: ACTIVE, RESTRICTED (some actions are refused by policy) or CLOSED.

username.description: The account's public username and the name of its /r/ link, or null until it picks one with PUT /v1/me/username. It can change. Servers before contract 129 omit it.

avatar_seed.description: Random seed assigned when the account is created; the account can change it with PUT /v1/me/avatar. Clients draw the account's generated avatar from it, so the avatar is the same on every device. Servers before contract 134 omit it.

picture_url.description: The picture the account's profile shows in place of the generated avatar, the same on every device and wherever the account appears (picture_source): the picture it uploaded with PUT /v1/me/picture/upload, else x_picture_url unless x_picture_shown is false. Absent when the profile shows the generated avatar. Servers before contract 186 omit it, and before contract 241 it is always x_picture_url.

picture_source.description: Where picture_url comes from: UPLOAD for the account's uploaded picture, X for its X picture, GENERATED when picture_url is absent and clients draw the avatar from avatar_seed. Servers before contract 241 omit it.

x_picture_url.description: The profile picture of the X account linked to the account's Privy login, whether or not the profile shows it. The server reads it from Privy on the first GET /v1/me after each sign-in and on POST /v1/me/picture, and serves what it last read: if Privy does not answer, the earlier picture stays until a later GET /v1/me reads it. Absent when the server has no picture: none is linked, it is not on X's profile picture hosts, it has not been read yet, or the server has no Privy app secret. Servers before contract 241 omit it.

x_picture_shown.description: Whether the profile shows x_picture_url when it has no uploaded picture: true until the account hides it with PUT /v1/me/picture/x, whether or not X is linked. Servers before contract 241 omit it.

wallet.description: The account's wallet: its Privy embedded wallet, or the one wallet of an account that signs in with an external wallet. It is the account's owner, which signs API-key issuance, and its signer, which signs its financial actions.

wallet_kind.description: EMBEDDED for a Privy embedded wallet, whose free vault cash Totalis moves to HyperCore in the background; EXTERNAL for an account that signs in with an external wallet, which has no such sweep. Servers before contract 147 omit it.

public_profile.description: Whether the account turned on its public trader profile with PUT /v1/me/public-profile. Servers before contract 190 omit it.

x_username.description: The handle of the X account linked to the account's Privy login, read from Privy with picture_url and served the same way. Absent when the server has none: none is linked, X does not allow it, it has not been read yet, or the server has no Privy app secret. Servers before contract 210 omit it.

x_shown.description: Whether the public trader profile shows x_username: true until the account hides it with PUT /v1/me/public-profile/x, whether or not X is linked. Servers before contract 210 omit it.

genesis.description: The account's Genesis Account badge (GET /v1/me/genesis), shown whether or not its public profile is on; absent until it is earned. Servers before contract 227 omit it.

admitted_at.description: When the partner first admitted the wallet; the same on every retry.

address.description: The wallet that may create its account at its next sign-in.

consent.description: The wallet's consent to this partner: its personal_sign of the exact message whose lines are `Allow <slug> to open a Totalis account for this wallet.`, `This does not authorize a financial action.`, an empty line, `Wallet: <lowercase address>`, `Partner: <slug>`, `Environment: <development|staging|production>`, `Chain ID: <chain>` and `Expires At: <expires_at>`, joined by newlines. The SDK builds it (admissionConsentMessage).

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC, after now and at most 24 hours ahead, signed exactly as sent.

signature.description: The wallet's personal_sign signature over the consent message.

chain_id.description: HyperEVM chain the approval is on.

vault.description: The vault whose WalletAccept is `spender`, GET /v1/deployment `vault_address`; an approval read for another vault does not fund an accept through this one.

token.description: The USDC contract the permit is signed for; its EIP-712 domain is GET /v1/deployment `usdc.eip712_domain`.

account.description: The account wallet, the permit's owner.

approved.description: Atomic USDC (6 decimals) the wallet still lets WalletAccept pull, as USDC `allowance(account, spender)`; null when unread.

nonce.description: The wallet's next USDC permit nonce, as USDC `nonces(account)`; null when unread.

block.description: HyperEVM block both values were read at; null when unread.

amount.description: Atomic USDC (6 decimals) the approval becomes, the permit's signed `value`; 0 revokes it.

deadline.description: Unix seconds after which USDC refuses the permit; a permit sent after it ends PERMIT_EXPIRED.

signature.description: The account wallet's EIP-712 signature over USDC's EIP-2612 Permit(owner, spender, value, nonce, deadline) in the USDC domain GET /v1/deployment publishes, with the account wallet as owner and GET /v1/me/wallet-approval `spender` and `nonce`.

request_id.description: The Idempotency-Key that first sent this permit.

operation_id.description: The USDC_PERMIT operation that relays it.

amount.description: The approval it sets, atomic USDC; 0 is a revoke.

nonce.description: The permit nonce it was signed with.

status.description: Its operation's status. Only COMMITTED set the approval; REVERTED and EXPIRED_UNEXECUTED changed nothing.

transaction_hash.description: HyperEVM hash of the transaction carrying it; null before it is broadcast.

reason.description: Why it changed nothing, present only once status is REVERTED or EXPIRED_UNEXECUTED. `PERMIT_EXPIRED`: its deadline passed first. `PERMIT_NONCE_USED`: another permit used its nonce first; read the approval before signing again, as it may already be what you wanted. `PERMIT_REVERTED`: USDC refused it for another reason.

challenge_id.description: Send it with the signature to POST /v1/auth/wallet-sessions.

message.description: The exact EIP-4361 message to sign with personal_sign.

issued_at.description: When the challenge was issued, RFC 3339 UTC.

expires_at.description: Five minutes after issued_at; exchange the signature before then.

WalletChallengeRequest.description: Asks for a SIWE message proving control of an externally owned wallet. The message names the origin, chain, nonce and the Idempotency-Key as its Request ID, and expires after 5 minutes.

address.description: The wallet signing in. An address holding contract code is refused with WALLET_CONTRACT_UNSUPPORTED.

origin.description: Must equal the request's Origin header exactly.

WalletSession.description: A bearer session for the wallet's account. It lasts at most 30 days and ends after 7 days without an API request, or at logout. It authenticates the account; every bet, cash-out and withdrawal still needs the wallet's own signature.

token_type.description: Always Bearer: send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

access_token.description: The session token. It works only with the Origin it signed in from; keep it out of URLs and logs.

address.description: The signed-in wallet, which is the account's wallet.

issued_at.description: When the session was issued, RFC 3339 UTC.

expires_at.description: The 30-day cap; the 7-day idle limit can end the session sooner.

WalletSessionRequest.description: Proves the challenge with the wallet's personal_sign signature over the exact message.

challenge_id.description: The challenge_id from POST /v1/auth/wallet-challenges; each proves one session.

signature.description: The wallet's personal_sign signature over the challenge's exact message.

destination.description: External address that receives the USDC.

amount.description: Total amount sent to destination, in atomic USDC (6 decimals).

shortfall_amount.description: Part of amount first withdrawn from the vault to the wallet, in atomic USDC; "0" when the wallet already covered it.
